journal_result.headline: The ERC-8004 Validation Registry IS live and fully callable on BSC at 0x8004Cc8439f36fd5F9F049D9fF86523Df6dAAB58 with zero usage anywhere, and enumeration needs no log scan at all because agentIds are contiguous from 0 and the exact count is one eth_getStorageAt.

verified.claim: Validation Registry is deployed on BSC mainnet, correctly wired, and fully functional (8004scan just does not list it)
verified.value: 0x8004Cc8439f36fd5F9F049D9fF86523Df6dAAB58, proxy 130 bytes, impl 0xDB31f5d9167f8ebc8B30FbBF814c4d297c2D7F99 (5876 bytes)
verified.how: cast codesize; cast call <addr> 'getIdentityRegistry()(address)' --rpc-url https://bsc-rpc.publicnode.com returns 0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432; getVersion() returns "2.0.0"

verified.claim: Canonical mainnet validation address comes from the official repo, not guesswork
verified.value: MAINNET_ADDRESSES.validationRegistry
verified.how: curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erc-8004/erc-8004-contracts/master/scripts/addresses.ts (line 81)

verified.claim: Validation writes are routed and guarded, so the contract is usable today
verified.value: validationRequest from agent owner would succeed; from a random EOA reverts 'Not authorized'; validator=0x0 reverts 'bad validator'; validationResponse on an unknown hash reverts 'unknown'
verified.how: cast call 0x8004Cc84... 'validationRequest(address,uint256,string,bytes32)' 0x1111... 1 'ipfs://q' 0x2222... --from 0x89E9E1ab11dD1B138b1dcE6d6A4a0926aaFD5029

verified.claim: Zero validations exist on BSC
verified.value: 0 agentIds with a validation request out of 1,999 checked (0-600 dense plus 1,400 stratified to 334,908), 0 unreadable
verified.how: batched eth_call of getAgentValidations(uint256) 0x8d5d0c2d, script three/research/tools/valscan.mjs

verified.claim: Zero validations and zero validators globally in 8004scan's index
verified.value: total_validations 0, total_validators 0, daily_validations 0
verified.how: curl -s https://api.8004scan.io/api/v1/stats/global

verified.claim: agentIds start at 0, not 1, and are contiguous

unverified.claim: The block at which each registry proxy was created
unverified.blocker: No Upgraded log on any of the three proxies in blocks 79,080,000 to 79,094,900, so creation predates the first registration. No free BSC RPC serves historical eth_getCode: publicnode refuses archive without a token, blxrbdn answers 'not supported', zan.top answers 'state ... is not available' for most old blocks. The first registration block 79,094,807 is verified and is the only block number a builder needs.

unverified.claim: The true total feedback count on BSC (8004scan's 11,719 figure from 2026-08-27)
unverified.blocker: Reproducing it needs a from-genesis log scan, and no free RPC gives both archive depth and a range above 10,000 blocks. The 388 figure here is a lower bound over a 2,098-agent sample, not a chain total.

unverified.claim: That FeedbackRevoked and ResponseAppended have ever fired on BSC
unverified.blocker: Zero revoked entries among 388 surveyed feedbacks and zero replies in 8004scan's chain-56 feedback list. Both functions are proven callable by simulation, but no real log could be located without a full archive scan.

unverified.claim: That agentWallet is cleared on transfer as an observed on-chain event
unverified.blocker: Read from source (_update writes "" and emits MetadataSet(id,"agentWallet","agentWallet","")) and consistent with the 1 empty value in 136 sampled ids, but no transfer occurred inside the 4,500-block window scanned, so there is no observed clearing log.

unverified.claim: That the deployed implementations are byte-identical to the repo source
unverified.blocker: The repo publishes no verified-source link and BscScan needs an API key. The match is inferred from an exact dispatch-table match, ERC-7201 slot constants equal to the source comments, getVersion() returning "2.0.0" and every revert string matching. Strong, not proof.

unverified.claim: Whether the Safe or the EOA has ever exercised the upgrade path
unverified.blocker: Needs the proxies' full Upgraded log history, blocked by the same archive range limit.

unverified.claim: Whether categories can be derived reliably from TermiX data
unverified.blocker: Every TermiX sample fetched reported termix.profile.category = "general", so the field exists but carries no signal in the sample. A larger TermiX sweep is needed before relying on it.

design_implications: Index from storage plus Multicall3, never from a log scan: one eth_getStorageAt at 0xa040f782729de4970518741823ec1276cbcd41a0c7493f62d173341566a04e00 gives the exact agent count, ids are contiguous from 0, and 670 eth_calls sweep every agent's tokenURI, ownerOf and getAgentWallet in about 30 minutes on a free RPC. Keep it fresh with a _lastId delta. Reserve eth_getLogs for the three NewFeedback fields that exist only in events (endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash).

Do not depend on 8004scan for BSC data: its indexer reports status down with its newest indexed BSC feedback five days stale at block 119,137,534 against head 120,025,025. Live RPC is fresher, and saying so with numbers is itself evidence for the Data Quality criterion.

Treat tokenURI as hostile input and ship six parsers: base64 data URI, gzip data URI (data:application/json;enc=gzip;level=6;base64), https, ipfs, empty, plus raw JSON with no prefix. Roughly 5% of agents hold something unparseable and roughly 5% of off-chain URIs 404 or return HTML, so every agent card needs a defined 'registration file unreadable' state with the reject count visible.

Read both spellings of the two flags that have two spellings: x402Support / x402support and supportedTrust / supportedTrusts. Each misspelling covers about 5% of documents, so ignoring them mislabels one agent in twenty on exactly the fields the sponsors score.

The four mandated categories must be derived, because no standard category field exists and getMetadata(id,'category') is populated on zero agents. Build a classifier over name, description, termix.tags, roles, attributes and OASF skill paths, then publish its rule set and per-category counts, since Agent Diversity is one of only three published criteria.

Surface reputation honestly or it will backfire: 388 entries over 299 of 2,098 sampled agents, 68% of them from one Telegram-advert spammer, every value at valueDecimals 0. A naive average puts the spammer on top. Use getClients then getSummary(agentId, clientAddresses, tag1, tag2) with client-count shown, and remember readAllFeedback with an empty client array is the only client-list-free on-chain read.

The Validation Registry is an open goal: deployed on BSC, correctly wired, callable, and used by nobody anywhere 8004scan indexes. Writing one real validationRequest plus one real validationResponse on BSC mainnet gives the submission an on-chain artifact no rival has, and it maps onto the TermiX rubric's proven-agent-advantage and high-stakes weightings. requestHash is caller-chosen and must be unique, response is 0..100, and validationResponse can be re-called on the same hash with different tags for progressive finality.

Record and monitor the upgrade risk: Identity and Reputation can be replaced by a 3-of-5 Safe at 0xF223968Dd0c66472E31043acAcCcF5D1464D644b, Validation by a single EOA at 0x8888d0A88ef8302dfa4BA53c41c2fE3c4E486f42. Pin the three implementation addresses seen at build time, read the EIP-1967 slot on every sync, and banner any change. One extra storage read per sweep.

setAgentWallet is the payment hook for x402 or B402 and its deadline window is exactly 300 seconds, with the signature required from the new wallet rather than the owner. Nobody on BSC has used it (all 541 non-zero agentWallet values in the sample still equal ownerOf), so getting it working is a demonstrable first.

Operator delegation is free product surface: every mutating identity call accepts isApprovedForAll(owner, msg.sender), so one setApprovalForAll(marketplace, true) lets the marketplace manage a user's whole fleet of URIs, metadata and wallets with no custody and no new contract.

Cross-chain support costs nothing: the same three addresses exist on 24 mainnets and 25 testnets from one CREATE2 factory, so an eip155:<chainId>:0x8004A169... key generalises with only an RPC URL per chain. BSC is the biggest registry at 334,924 agents, which is the argument for BSC being the marketplace's home.

design_implications: Index from storage plus Multicall3, never from a log scan: one eth_getStorageAt at 0xa040f782729de4970518741823ec1276cbcd41a0c7493f62d173341566a04e00 gives the exact agent count, ids are contiguous from 0, and 670 eth_calls sweep every agent's tokenURI, ownerOf and getAgentWallet in about 30 minutes on a free RPC. Keep it fresh with a _lastId delta. Reserve eth_getLogs for the three NewFeedback fields that exist only in events (endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash).

Do not depend on 8004scan for BSC data: its indexer reports status down with its newest indexed BSC feedback five days stale at block 119,137,534 against head 120,025,025. Live RPC is fresher, and saying so with numbers is itself evidence for the Data Quality criterion.

Treat tokenURI as hostile input and ship six parsers: base64 data URI, gzip data URI (data:application/json;enc=gzip;level=6;base64), https, ipfs, empty, plus raw JSON with no prefix. Roughly 5% of agents hold something unparseable and roughly 5% of off-chain URIs 404 or return HTML, so every agent card needs a defined 'registration file unreadable' state with the reject count visible.

Read both spellings of the two flags that have two spellings: x402Support / x402support and supportedTrust / supportedTrusts. Each misspelling covers about 5% of documents, so ignoring them mislabels one agent in twenty on exactly the fields the sponsors score.

The four mandated categories must be derived, because no standard category field exists and getMetadata(id,'category') is populated on zero agents. Build a classifier over name, description, termix.tags, roles, attributes and OASF skill paths, then publish its rule set and per-category counts, since Agent Diversity is one of only three published criteria.

Surface reputation honestly or it will backfire: 388 entries over 299 of 2,098 sampled agents, 68% of them from one Telegram-advert spammer, every value at valueDecimals 0. A naive average puts the spammer on top. Use getClients then getSummary(agentId, clientAddresses, tag1, tag2) with client-count shown, and remember readAllFeedback with an empty client array is the only client-list-free on-chain read.

The Validation Registry is an open goal: deployed on BSC, correctly wired, callable, and used by nobody anywhere 8004scan indexes. Writing one real validationRequest plus one real validationResponse on BSC mainnet gives the submission an on-chain artifact no rival has, and it maps onto the TermiX rubric's proven-agent-advantage and high-stakes weightings. requestHash is caller-chosen and must be unique, response is 0..100, and validationResponse can be re-called on the same hash with different tags for progressive finality.

Record and monitor the upgrade risk: Identity and Reputation can be replaced by a 3-of-5 Safe at 0xF223968Dd0c66472E31043acAcCcF5D1464D644b, Validation by a single EOA at 0x8888d0A88ef8302dfa4BA53c41c2fE3c4E486f42. Pin the three implementation addresses seen at build time, read the EIP-1967 slot on every sync, and banner any change. One extra storage read per sweep.

setAgentWallet is the payment hook for x402 or B402 and its deadline window is exactly 300 seconds, with the signature required from the new wallet rather than the owner. Nobody on BSC has used it (all 541 non-zero agentWallet values in the sample still equal ownerOf), so getting it working is a demonstrable first.

Operator delegation is free product surface: every mutating identity call accepts isApprovedForAll(owner, msg.sender), so one setApprovalForAll(marketplace, true) lets the marketplace manage a user's whole fleet of URIs, metadata and wallets with no custody and no new contract.

Cross-chain support costs nothing: the same three addresses exist on 24 mainnets and 25 testnets from one CREATE2 factory, so an eip155:<chainId>:0x8004A169... key generalises with only an RPC URL per chain. BSC is the biggest registry at 334,924 agents, which is the argument for BSC being the marketplace's home.

design_implications: Build to x402 v2, not v1. B402's V2 endpoint rejects any other x402Version with invalid_x402_version, and v2 is the current spec. Emit PAYMENT-REQUIRED on the 402, read PAYMENT-SIGNATURE on the retry, return PAYMENT-RESPONSE. Where a B402 doc line asks for X-PAYMENT-REQUIREMENTS instead, send both headers: B402 never reads the buyer-facing 402, only the merchant's own /verify body.

Do not block the build on B402 credentials. Write the resource server against a FacilitatorClient interface with two implementations, an in-process facilitator we control and a B402 HTTP client. The demo runs on the first, the second is a config flip if credentials land. Our prior paywall already has exactly this shape in src/payments/facilitator.py.

A self-hosted facilitator on BSC works today with the official SDK unpatched. register_exact_evm_facilitator(f, signer, networks="eip155:56") plus correct extra.name and extra.version is enough, because get_network_config falls back to a bare chain_id and the exact-EVM facilitator takes the EIP-712 domain from the requirements.

Price the demo in USD1. It is the only BSC token where native EIP-3009 is verified on chain, the canonical typehashes are exposed and match, ERC-5267 eip712Domain() is available so the domain can be read rather than guessed, and the Bazaar's own traffic is already concentrated (97 of the first 100 listings). Truly gasless for the buyer including the first call.

Never hardcode extra.name. Read it. U's ERC-20 name() is "United Stables" while Binance's example shows "U", and on testnet the same brand really is "U". Resolve it at startup from ERC-5267 eip712Domain() when present, otherwise brute force the domain separator against candidate name and version pairs and fail loudly on no match. Two RPC calls remove the whole class of invalid_exact_evm_payload_signature failures.

Read decimals() per token per environment and keep atomic amounts as strings. Mainnet is 18 across all four tokens, testnet is 6, 6 and 18. Binance shipped this wrong in their own docs for about a month, and merchants pricing at 10000 for one cent were charging 1e-14 of a token.

Support both transfer methods or narrow the token list. Pricing in USDT or USDC (what agents on BSC actually hold) makes Permit2 mandatory, and the buyer's first payment per token needs a one-time approve(Permit2, max) that costs the buyer BNB gas. Detect a missing allowance before signing, surface the approval as an explicit onboarding step, and do not advertise that path as gasless.

Treat settlement as asynchronous from day one. Poll /settle at 3 to 5 s well past maxTimeoutSeconds (the backend reconciles for up to about 30 minutes), key the outcome on whether transaction is empty, and hold the resource until success is true. Enforce our own idempotency on (nonce, network, payer) rather than only trusting the facilitator's.

Use receiveWithAuthorization the moment any contract of ours holds the funds. transferWithAuthorization is correct for a facilitator EOA paying straight to the seller. An escrow, a fee split or a marketplace vault hits the ERC-3009 front-running case that only the payee guard closes. USD1 implements the guard, verified on chain.

The upto scheme is the right primitive for metered agent work. A rebalancing or yield agent cannot know its cost before running, so the buyer authorizes a ceiling once and is charged the true amount at settle via settleAmount. It is a B402 extension rather than core spec, but the canonical x402UptoPermit2Proxy is already deployed on BSC so the primitive exists either way.

Read the B402 Bazaar, do not duplicate it. 979 live BSC resources, public and unauthenticated, with per-resource 30-day call counts and unique-payer counts. Ingesting it gives the marketplace a populated catalog on day one and gives the Data Quality criterion something measurable. Budget for a normalizing adapter, because the live shape puts the transfer method in scheme and uses maxAmountRequired.

Listing our own agents in the Bazaar rides on settlement, not registration. Attach extensions.bazaar to every V2 settle and the endpoint becomes agent-discoverable. It requires B402 credentials and a real settle, which is a reason to get testnet credentials early even if mainnet does not land, and a reason to treat it as a stretch goal rather than a dependency.

Pin the spec copy we cite. Two live copies of the v2 specification differ and Binance links the smaller coinbase one, which lacks PAYMENT-REQUIRED and settlement_pending entirely. Cite x402-foundation/x402 with today's date and keep the raw capture so a judge can see which text we built against.

Watch the b402 name collision. An unrelated project uses the same name across a docs site, npm and GitHub. Every dependency must come from Binance's documented surface or from x402 Foundation packages, never from a package that merely matches the name.

design_implications: Build to x402 v2, not v1. B402's V2 endpoint rejects any other x402Version with invalid_x402_version, and v2 is the current spec. Emit PAYMENT-REQUIRED on the 402, read PAYMENT-SIGNATURE on the retry, return PAYMENT-RESPONSE. Where a B402 doc line asks for X-PAYMENT-REQUIREMENTS instead, send both headers: B402 never reads the buyer-facing 402, only the merchant's own /verify body.

Do not block the build on B402 credentials. Write the resource server against a FacilitatorClient interface with two implementations, an in-process facilitator we control and a B402 HTTP client. The demo runs on the first, the second is a config flip if credentials land. Our prior paywall already has exactly this shape in src/payments/facilitator.py.

A self-hosted facilitator on BSC works today with the official SDK unpatched. register_exact_evm_facilitator(f, signer, networks="eip155:56") plus correct extra.name and extra.version is enough, because get_network_config falls back to a bare chain_id and the exact-EVM facilitator takes the EIP-712 domain from the requirements.

Price the demo in USD1. It is the only BSC token where native EIP-3009 is verified on chain, the canonical typehashes are exposed and match, ERC-5267 eip712Domain() is available so the domain can be read rather than guessed, and the Bazaar's own traffic is already concentrated (97 of the first 100 listings). Truly gasless for the buyer including the first call.

Never hardcode extra.name. Read it. U's ERC-20 name() is "United Stables" while Binance's example shows "U", and on testnet the same brand really is "U". Resolve it at startup from ERC-5267 eip712Domain() when present, otherwise brute force the domain separator against candidate name and version pairs and fail loudly on no match. Two RPC calls remove the whole class of invalid_exact_evm_payload_signature failures.

Read decimals() per token per environment and keep atomic amounts as strings. Mainnet is 18 across all four tokens, testnet is 6, 6 and 18. Binance shipped this wrong in their own docs for about a month, and merchants pricing at 10000 for one cent were charging 1e-14 of a token.

Support both transfer methods or narrow the token list. Pricing in USDT or USDC (what agents on BSC actually hold) makes Permit2 mandatory, and the buyer's first payment per token needs a one-time approve(Permit2, max) that costs the buyer BNB gas. Detect a missing allowance before signing, surface the approval as an explicit onboarding step, and do not advertise that path as gasless.

Treat settlement as asynchronous from day one. Poll /settle at 3 to 5 s well past maxTimeoutSeconds (the backend reconciles for up to about 30 minutes), key the outcome on whether transaction is empty, and hold the resource until success is true. Enforce our own idempotency on (nonce, network, payer) rather than only trusting the facilitator's.

Use receiveWithAuthorization the moment any contract of ours holds the funds. transferWithAuthorization is correct for a facilitator EOA paying straight to the seller. An escrow, a fee split or a marketplace vault hits the ERC-3009 front-running case that only the payee guard closes. USD1 implements the guard, verified on chain.

The upto scheme is the right primitive for metered agent work. A rebalancing or yield agent cannot know its cost before running, so the buyer authorizes a ceiling once and is charged the true amount at settle via settleAmount. It is a B402 extension rather than core spec, but the canonical x402UptoPermit2Proxy is already deployed on BSC so the primitive exists either way.

Read the B402 Bazaar, do not duplicate it. 979 live BSC resources, public and unauthenticated, with per-resource 30-day call counts and unique-payer counts. Ingesting it gives the marketplace a populated catalog on day one and gives the Data Quality criterion something measurable. Budget for a normalizing adapter, because the live shape puts the transfer method in scheme and uses maxAmountRequired.

Listing our own agents in the Bazaar rides on settlement, not registration. Attach extensions.bazaar to every V2 settle and the endpoint becomes agent-discoverable. It requires B402 credentials and a real settle, which is a reason to get testnet credentials early even if mainnet does not land, and a reason to treat it as a stretch goal rather than a dependency.

Pin the spec copy we cite. Two live copies of the v2 specification differ and Binance links the smaller coinbase one, which lacks PAYMENT-REQUIRED and settlement_pending entirely. Cite x402-foundation/x402 with today's date and keep the raw capture so a judge can see which text we built against.

Watch the b402 name collision. An unrelated project uses the same name across a docs site, npm and GitHub. Every dependency must come from Binance's documented surface or from x402 Foundation packages, never from a package that merely matches the name.

design_implications: Never call Venus's getAccountLiquidity 'borrowing power'. It is the liquidation check under the liquidation threshold. getBorrowingPower is the borrow-capacity check under the collateral factor. On a real account today the two differ by $29.81 on $825 of debt, 3.9 percent of collateral value, and a market like vLINK with CF 0 and LT 0.63 contributes seizable collateral while contributing nothing to borrow capacity.

Read risk weights per account, not per market: getEffectiveLtvFactor(account, vToken, 0|1) and getEffectiveLiquidationIncentive(account, vToken). getCollateralFactor and getLiquidationThreshold return core-pool values and are wrong for any account with userPoolId != 0, and inside Venus E-Mode pool 1 the liquidation penalty is 6 percent rather than the core pool's 10 percent.

Pin every position recompute to one block number. An unpinned Venus run disagreed with the chain by 2.9e16 wei on both the CF and LT paths, an identical offset that reads as a formula bug but was six blocks of drift at 0.45 s per block.

Tag every rate with its unit. Venus is 1e18 per block annualised over 70,080,000, Lista Lending is 1e18 per second annualised as exp(r*31536000)-1, Aave is already per year in ray, Lista CDP is a per-second ray exponent over a 31,556,952 second year. Storing '4.58' throws away the only thing that made it checkable.

Publish measured and advertised yield side by side and reconcile them. Venus's own APY needs the Compound-inherited exponent 364, not 365, to match venus.io to 4e-12. PancakeSwap's feeUSD24h/tvlUSD overstates LP yield by exactly feeProtocol/10000, which is 33 percent on the 0.01 percent tier, so 42.34 percent gross becomes 28.37 percent net.

Build the health-factor loop as a price watcher plus precomputed per-account trigger prices, not a recompute loop. Only the oracle can move a healthy position to liquidatable in one step; interest accrual at vUSDT's rate needs 15.6 million blocks (about 81 days) to grow the debt 1 percent, and every risk parameter changes on governance only.

Watch the Lista CDP stored spot separately from the live oracle. Liquidation eligibility is Dog.bark's ink*spot < art*rate against the poked spot, which sat 0.229 percent above the live pip. Treat 'live price crossed my liquidation price' as the alarm and 'spot poked' as the deadline, and note poke is permissionless so the agent can trigger it itself.

Scope agent sessions by selector and not by contract, and constrain the beneficiary argument. repayBorrowBehalf and mintBehalf on Venus, repay and supplyCollateral on Moolah, payback and deposit on Interaction only reduce risk; redeem, withdrawCollateral, borrow, exitMarket, Vat.hope and Moolah.setAuthorization hand over the position. If the session mechanism cannot constrain calldata, put a forwarder that hardcodes the beneficiary behind the allowlist.

Ship two zero-custody remedies that move no tokens at all: Venus enterPool(uint96), which can lift slisBNB's liquidation threshold from 0.800 in core to 0.930 in pool 3 after hasValidPoolBorrows clears it, and Interaction.poke, which makes the agent's own health read authoritative. Neither needs a spend cap and no rival agent will be doing the first.

Use Lista's flash loan for the atomic self-liquidation demo. Moolah.flashLoan is permissionless, fee-free and gated only by flashLoanTokenBlacklist, while Venus's executeFlashLoan sits behind setWhiteListFlashLoanAccount and setFlashLoanPaused.

Never hardcode 1e36 in a Moolah health check. collateralPrice is scaled 10^(36 + loanDecimals - collateralDecimals) and it only collapsed to 1e36 in my three samples because all six tokens were 18 decimals. Also call brokers(id) first: on a broker market _isHealthy substitutes the broker's total debt and a broker-specific price, so market() plus position() cannot reconstruct health.

Read lltv and every risk parameter from chain, never from a docs table. Lista's delayed-liquidation page lists BTCB/USDT at 'Original LLTV 80%' while idToMarketParams on that id returns 0.86, and Lista's documented minimum LIF of 1.048 does not exist in Moolah.liquidate, which returns 1.0438 for lltv 0.86.

Handle Venus isolated pools as a separate ABI, not a variant. markets(address) returns three fields with lt in place of isVenus, liquidationIncentiveMantissa exists there, and minLiquidatableCollateral of 100e18 means a small position needs a full liquidation rather than a close-factor-limited partial, so a planned 50 percent repay is the wrong transaction.

Define track record before building it: every fill resolves to a txHash with (blockNumber, transactionIndex, logIndex) as the ordering key, the window is the agent's whole life with both endpoints and the trade count, a hold-the-starting-inventory benchmark is marked at the same two blocks, and risk is reported as max drawdown, realised volatility, peak notional and worst health factor. Win rate must be per round trip, because a grid bot's individual fills are wins by construction.

Store the oracle mark alongside the execution price on every fill. The Venus ResilientOracle gives a free independent mark for 55 BSC assets, which is what turns 'we filled' into 'we filled at a good price' and lets any visitor re-derive every published number from BSC alone.

Surface only venues where a live read backs every number shown. Venus core plus 8 isolated pools plus 15 E-Mode pools, Lista Lending, Lista CDP and Aave v3 BSC are all verified here. Kinza, Avalon and Euler on BNB Chain are worth adding for breadth but their addresses could not be read from a primary source this pass.

Budget for the RPC ceiling. Free public BSC endpoints serve no archive state past roughly the last hundred blocks and cap eth_getLogs near 4,500 blocks, so any historical track record, LST yield derivation or liquidation history needs a paid archive endpoint or a persisted local index built forward from launch.

design_implications: Never call Venus's getAccountLiquidity 'borrowing power'. It is the liquidation check under the liquidation threshold. getBorrowingPower is the borrow-capacity check under the collateral factor. On a real account today the two differ by $29.81 on $825 of debt, 3.9 percent of collateral value, and a market like vLINK with CF 0 and LT 0.63 contributes seizable collateral while contributing nothing to borrow capacity.

Read risk weights per account, not per market: getEffectiveLtvFactor(account, vToken, 0|1) and getEffectiveLiquidationIncentive(account, vToken). getCollateralFactor and getLiquidationThreshold return core-pool values and are wrong for any account with userPoolId != 0, and inside Venus E-Mode pool 1 the liquidation penalty is 6 percent rather than the core pool's 10 percent.

Pin every position recompute to one block number. An unpinned Venus run disagreed with the chain by 2.9e16 wei on both the CF and LT paths, an identical offset that reads as a formula bug but was six blocks of drift at 0.45 s per block.

Tag every rate with its unit. Venus is 1e18 per block annualised over 70,080,000, Lista Lending is 1e18 per second annualised as exp(r*31536000)-1, Aave is already per year in ray, Lista CDP is a per-second ray exponent over a 31,556,952 second year. Storing '4.58' throws away the only thing that made it checkable.

Publish measured and advertised yield side by side and reconcile them. Venus's own APY needs the Compound-inherited exponent 364, not 365, to match venus.io to 4e-12. PancakeSwap's feeUSD24h/tvlUSD overstates LP yield by exactly feeProtocol/10000, which is 33 percent on the 0.01 percent tier, so 42.34 percent gross becomes 28.37 percent net.

Build the health-factor loop as a price watcher plus precomputed per-account trigger prices, not a recompute loop. Only the oracle can move a healthy position to liquidatable in one step; interest accrual at vUSDT's rate needs 15.6 million blocks (about 81 days) to grow the debt 1 percent, and every risk parameter changes on governance only.

Watch the Lista CDP stored spot separately from the live oracle. Liquidation eligibility is Dog.bark's ink*spot < art*rate against the poked spot, which sat 0.229 percent above the live pip. Treat 'live price crossed my liquidation price' as the alarm and 'spot poked' as the deadline, and note poke is permissionless so the agent can trigger it itself.

Scope agent sessions by selector and not by contract, and constrain the beneficiary argument. repayBorrowBehalf and mintBehalf on Venus, repay and supplyCollateral on Moolah, payback and deposit on Interaction only reduce risk; redeem, withdrawCollateral, borrow, exitMarket, Vat.hope and Moolah.setAuthorization hand over the position. If the session mechanism cannot constrain calldata, put a forwarder that hardcodes the beneficiary behind the allowlist.

Ship two zero-custody remedies that move no tokens at all: Venus enterPool(uint96), which can lift slisBNB's liquidation threshold from 0.800 in core to 0.930 in pool 3 after hasValidPoolBorrows clears it, and Interaction.poke, which makes the agent's own health read authoritative. Neither needs a spend cap and no rival agent will be doing the first.

Use Lista's flash loan for the atomic self-liquidation demo. Moolah.flashLoan is permissionless, fee-free and gated only by flashLoanTokenBlacklist, while Venus's executeFlashLoan sits behind setWhiteListFlashLoanAccount and setFlashLoanPaused.

Never hardcode 1e36 in a Moolah health check. collateralPrice is scaled 10^(36 + loanDecimals - collateralDecimals) and it only collapsed to 1e36 in my three samples because all six tokens were 18 decimals. Also call brokers(id) first: on a broker market _isHealthy substitutes the broker's total debt and a broker-specific price, so market() plus position() cannot reconstruct health.

Read lltv and every risk parameter from chain, never from a docs table. Lista's delayed-liquidation page lists BTCB/USDT at 'Original LLTV 80%' while idToMarketParams on that id returns 0.86, and Lista's documented minimum LIF of 1.048 does not exist in Moolah.liquidate, which returns 1.0438 for lltv 0.86.

Handle Venus isolated pools as a separate ABI, not a variant. markets(address) returns three fields with lt in place of isVenus, liquidationIncentiveMantissa exists there, and minLiquidatableCollateral of 100e18 means a small position needs a full liquidation rather than a close-factor-limited partial, so a planned 50 percent repay is the wrong transaction.

Define track record before building it: every fill resolves to a txHash with (blockNumber, transactionIndex, logIndex) as the ordering key, the window is the agent's whole life with both endpoints and the trade count, a hold-the-starting-inventory benchmark is marked at the same two blocks, and risk is reported as max drawdown, realised volatility, peak notional and worst health factor. Win rate must be per round trip, because a grid bot's individual fills are wins by construction.

Store the oracle mark alongside the execution price on every fill. The Venus ResilientOracle gives a free independent mark for 55 BSC assets, which is what turns 'we filled' into 'we filled at a good price' and lets any visitor re-derive every published number from BSC alone.

Surface only venues where a live read backs every number shown. Venus core plus 8 isolated pools plus 15 E-Mode pools, Lista Lending, Lista CDP and Aave v3 BSC are all verified here. Kinza, Avalon and Euler on BNB Chain are worth adding for breadth but their addresses could not be read from a primary source this pass.

Budget for the RPC ceiling. Free public BSC endpoints serve no archive state past roughly the last hundred blocks and cap eth_getLogs near 4,500 blocks, so any historical track record, LST yield derivation or liquidation history needs a paid archive endpoint or a persisted local index built forward from launch.

design_implications: Publish the agent count from the registry counter with its block height and timestamp, not from an indexer. One eth_getStorageAt gives 334,935; 8004scan gives 303,461 from a 32-hour-old checkpoint and its own two endpoints disagree by 820. Showing both rows with the lag turns a discrepancy into a differentiating feature, and a judge who checks the number will check it on chain.

Make callability the product, because it is the scarce thing. 233 of 600 declare a concrete endpoint, 230 answer, 218 of those answer with a web page for humans, 12 answer as an API and 0 answer with a payment challenge. Listing 334,935 agents is a directory; ranking the 2% a machine can actually call, and saying why the rest fail, is the listing that carries information.

Compute liveness yourself and stamp the age of the check. The registry has no liveness field, and the one indexer that has one scores ClawNews 100 out of 100 while its TLS certificate does not match its own hostname and its verification error has sat unrefreshed for 108 days. Store the probe result, timestamp, HTTP status, TLS verdict and DNS verdict per endpoint.

Separate the four failure modes and never merge them into "offline": DNS does not resolve (2 of 600), TLS name mismatch (clawnews.io), HTTP 404 from a live host (bitagent.io, twice), and template placeholder never substituted (51 of 600). Each needs a different fix from the operator, so merging them destroys the actionable part.

Do not filter on agentWallet != 0; it passes the entire registry, because register writes msg.sender into the wallet slot at mint. The filter with signal is getAgentWallet(id) != ownerOf(id), which currently matches 0 of 600. Until someone sets one, price and payment destination must come from the endpoint's 402 challenge, not the registry.

Resolve vendor endpoint templates and say that you did. The 51 Termix agents publish {agentId} with an empty registrations array so no conforming client can call them; substituting the token id returns a card, and every card sampled says UNBOUND with a null endpoint. Resolving the template converts 51 dead rows into 51 honest "registered but not bound" rows.

Do not source the four mandated categories from registry keyword search. The whole index yields 47 rebalancing, 20 grid, 430 apy, 21 health factor: 518 agents at the most generous reading, 0.17%, and the 600-agent sample contains one. The categories have to be populated with agents the marketplace itself runs or onboards, and the census is the defensible argument for why.

Do not resell the ERC-8004 reputation layer as performance evidence. 4,406 of 334,935 agents have any feedback, 111 addresses wrote all 29,712 rows, the top 100 agents hold 52% of them, and 844 of 950 sampled rows tag personality, knowledge, relationship, style, stance or timeline while zero tag a financial outcome. A TermiX-style "proven agent advantage" claim cannot be satisfied from this data, so the marketplace must generate its own outcome records.

Show the indexer shortfall as a first-class number: 8004scan holds 39.6% of the on-chain feedback and 90.6% of the on-chain agents, each checkable in one command. Reconciling the two sources costs two commands and is a cheap, verifiable claim to own.

Deduplicate by tokenURI bytes, not by name or owner. 215 of 600 share one byte-identical data: URI across 215 distinct owner addresses, so owner-based dedup fails and name-based dedup catches only the exact string. Hashing the tokenURI collapses the block in one pass, and 322 distinct names with 312 singletons is the real Agent Diversity number to report.

Build the endpoint parser to tolerate the wild, not the spec: services is the spec key but endpoints and a bare url also appear, x402Support competes with x402support, and supportedTrust with supportedTrusts. A parser that reads only the spec spelling silently drops rows, and 316 of 600 agents declare no service at all.

Plan the data pipeline around the RPC constraints measured here: full-history eth_getLogs needs a paid provider, whole-chain state can be swept with eth_call at 200 per batch against bsc.rpc.blxrbdn.com in about four minutes, publicnode returns HTTP 429 with a complete correct body so a status-only check throws away good data, and every bsc-dataseed host silently truncates a batch to one result.

design_implications: Publish the agent count from the registry counter with its block height and timestamp, not from an indexer. One eth_getStorageAt gives 334,935; 8004scan gives 303,461 from a 32-hour-old checkpoint and its own two endpoints disagree by 820. Showing both rows with the lag turns a discrepancy into a differentiating feature, and a judge who checks the number will check it on chain.

Make callability the product, because it is the scarce thing. 233 of 600 declare a concrete endpoint, 230 answer, 218 of those answer with a web page for humans, 12 answer as an API and 0 answer with a payment challenge. Listing 334,935 agents is a directory; ranking the 2% a machine can actually call, and saying why the rest fail, is the listing that carries information.

Compute liveness yourself and stamp the age of the check. The registry has no liveness field, and the one indexer that has one scores ClawNews 100 out of 100 while its TLS certificate does not match its own hostname and its verification error has sat unrefreshed for 108 days. Store the probe result, timestamp, HTTP status, TLS verdict and DNS verdict per endpoint.

Separate the four failure modes and never merge them into "offline": DNS does not resolve (2 of 600), TLS name mismatch (clawnews.io), HTTP 404 from a live host (bitagent.io, twice), and template placeholder never substituted (51 of 600). Each needs a different fix from the operator, so merging them destroys the actionable part.

Do not filter on agentWallet != 0; it passes the entire registry, because register writes msg.sender into the wallet slot at mint. The filter with signal is getAgentWallet(id) != ownerOf(id), which currently matches 0 of 600. Until someone sets one, price and payment destination must come from the endpoint's 402 challenge, not the registry.

Resolve vendor endpoint templates and say that you did. The 51 Termix agents publish {agentId} with an empty registrations array so no conforming client can call them; substituting the token id returns a card, and every card sampled says UNBOUND with a null endpoint. Resolving the template converts 51 dead rows into 51 honest "registered but not bound" rows.

Do not source the four mandated categories from registry keyword search. The whole index yields 47 rebalancing, 20 grid, 430 apy, 21 health factor: 518 agents at the most generous reading, 0.17%, and the 600-agent sample contains one. The categories have to be populated with agents the marketplace itself runs or onboards, and the census is the defensible argument for why.

Do not resell the ERC-8004 reputation layer as performance evidence. 4,406 of 334,935 agents have any feedback, 111 addresses wrote all 29,712 rows, the top 100 agents hold 52% of them, and 844 of 950 sampled rows tag personality, knowledge, relationship, style, stance or timeline while zero tag a financial outcome. A TermiX-style "proven agent advantage" claim cannot be satisfied from this data, so the marketplace must generate its own outcome records.

Show the indexer shortfall as a first-class number: 8004scan holds 39.6% of the on-chain feedback and 90.6% of the on-chain agents, each checkable in one command. Reconciling the two sources costs two commands and is a cheap, verifiable claim to own.

Deduplicate by tokenURI bytes, not by name or owner. 215 of 600 share one byte-identical data: URI across 215 distinct owner addresses, so owner-based dedup fails and name-based dedup catches only the exact string. Hashing the tokenURI collapses the block in one pass, and 322 distinct names with 312 singletons is the real Agent Diversity number to report.

Build the endpoint parser to tolerate the wild, not the spec: services is the spec key but endpoints and a bare url also appear, x402Support competes with x402support, and supportedTrust with supportedTrusts. A parser that reads only the spec spelling silently drops rows, and 316 of 600 agents declare no service at all.

Plan the data pipeline around the RPC constraints measured here: full-history eth_getLogs needs a paid provider, whole-chain state can be swept with eth_call at 200 per batch against bsc.rpc.blxrbdn.com in about four minutes, publicnode returns HTTP 429 with a complete correct body so a status-only check throws away good data, and every bsc-dataseed host silently truncates a batch to one result.

design_implications: Build the PancakeSwap agent as a range-health and rebalance agent that is right where the official tooling is wrong. It covers rebalancing directly and yield through CAKE/Merkl/Incentra, and it feeds the health-factor and grid agents the same pool state and swap path. Per position return principal, uncollected fees, pendingCake, in-range fraction, 7d fee APR, CAKE APR, extra APR, IL at the user's own scenarios and a verdict (hold/widen/narrow/recentre/exit) with the break-even arithmetic shown.

Correct IL is the single strongest Data Quality claim available. PancakeSwap's own liquidity-planner publishes 0% IL at 5x for full range (correct: -25.46%) and 0.03% at 2x for a +/-10% range (correct: -30.66%, a factor of 1000). Compute IL from the value function, not a lookup table, and show the capital-efficiency multiplier beside it so the user sees that concentrating 20x also multiplies IL 5x.

Compute CAKE farm APR on lmPool.lmLiquidity(), never on MasterChefV3 poolInfo.totalLiquidity and never on TVL. 48.95% of staked liquidity in the pool measured is out of range and earning nothing, so the wrong basis roughly halves the answer.

Compute fee APR net of the per-tier protocol fee read from slot0.feeProtocol at runtime. The 0.01% tier pays LPs 0.0067%, the 0.05% tier 0.033%, the 0.25% tier 0.17%, the 1% tier 0.68%. Read both directions (feeProtocol0 and feeProtocol1) rather than assuming symmetry, because setFeeProtocol can set them independently.

Pin every read in a position report to one block number, via a single batch or multicall. Three blocks of skew (2.25 s) moved amount0 by 0.63 bps, and the BNB/USDT mid moved 27 bps in 190 s. Mixed-block reads produce a number that never existed on chain.

Verify by simulation before showing a number. eth_call NFPM.collect and NFPM.decreaseLiquidity from the position owner and compare against the computed values. All four reconciled to the wei at a pinned block, which makes 'reconciles to chain' a badge a judge can check in one command and an agent can mark degraded when it fails.

Never gate a swap on best.priceImpactBps. Compute impact as 1 - (outputAmount/inputAmount)/mid with mid from sqrtPriceX96 on the deepest pool, use the API value only as a cross-check, and reject when the two disagree beyond tolerance. Gating on the raw field would refuse every small trade.

Cap the deadline yourself at 30 to 60 s and re-quote. Quote TTL is 180 s and the calldata deadline came back at expiresAt + 121 s, while the mid moved 27 bps in 190 s against a 50 bps execution floor.

Read the router `to` from a live /v1/calldata response at startup and allowlist that, plus the known historical routers, with a hard reject otherwise. Three different routers are in play and the official 8183 example's hardcoded allowlist plus its aggregator base are both stale against today's API.

Ship two modes rather than one compromise: plan mode that stops at a deep link (PancakeSwap's own skills do exactly this and carry zero risk) and execute mode behind the 14 guardrails their erc-8183-example enumerates. Show the guardrail list in the product. Recipient invariant, token safelist on endpoints only, minOut > 0, freshness re-quote, execution floor max(userMinOut, quote*(1-slippage)), deadline cap, per-job value cap, router allowlist, no standing approval, pull not push, refund on revert, measured balance delta not reported success, idempotency, no admin calls. That list maps almost one to one onto the Altana session gate (call allowlist, spend cap, expiry).

Route sends through https://bscrpc.pancakeswap.finance (PancakeSwap MEV Guard, free, first party, verified live) and budget 4 to 5 seconds of extra confirmation. Prefer the PancakeSwap X pcsx branch when a quote offers it, since a signed permit that never enters a mempool makes sandwiching structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.

Run our own sampler, because the free surface cannot supply history. No public BSC RPC serves state older than 60 to 82 blocks, the pool oracle maxes out at 10.9 h of lookback, the Explorer has no positions endpoint and no historical secondsInside. Poll snapshotCumulativesInside, pool.liquidity(), lmPool.lmLiquidity() and slot0 on the covered pools on a fixed cadence and retain 30 days. That store is the moat and it costs a few dozen keyless eth_calls a minute.

Cover v2 and v3 first, Infinity CL second, and say so. Infinity CL has real $2.0M to $2.3M pools, but the deepest pair still lives on v2 ($83.1M) and v3 ($11.6M for WBNB/USDT 0.01% alone) while Infinity WBNB/USDT pools hold under $1100. An agent that speaks only Infinity has almost nothing to manage.

Handle dynamic-fee Infinity pools honestly. fee = 0x800000 with lpFee = 0 means the hook sets the fee per swap, so there is no static tier to print. Fall back to realised fees from the Explorer aggregates or observed getFeeGrowthGlobals rather than fabricating a tier.
Rank pools on volumeUSD7d / tvlUSD, never on TVL. Two live v3 pools with $21.1M and $19.7M TVL had $277 and $634 of 24h volume and effectively zero APR.

Do not port Uniswap assumptions. There is no 0.3% tier on PancakeSwap v3 (feeAmountTickSpacing(3000) returns 0), slot0.feeProtocol is uint32 with a 65536 split and a 10000 denominator rather than Uniswap's uint8 nibbles, the Infinity protocol fee is added on top of the LP fee rather than carved out of it, CAKE's symbol() returns 'Cake', and PancakeSwap's Permit2 is a different contract from Uniswap's.

Gas being near free on BSC (0.05 gwei, $0.027 for a 738k-gas swap) shifts the rebalance calculus. The binding constraints are realised IL and the rebalancing swap cost, not gas, so an agent can afford to rebalance far more often here than the Ethereum literature assumes.

design_implications: Build the PancakeSwap agent as a range-health and rebalance agent that is right where the official tooling is wrong. It covers rebalancing directly and yield through CAKE/Merkl/Incentra, and it feeds the health-factor and grid agents the same pool state and swap path. Per position return principal, uncollected fees, pendingCake, in-range fraction, 7d fee APR, CAKE APR, extra APR, IL at the user's own scenarios and a verdict (hold/widen/narrow/recentre/exit) with the break-even arithmetic shown.

Correct IL is the single strongest Data Quality claim available. PancakeSwap's own liquidity-planner publishes 0% IL at 5x for full range (correct: -25.46%) and 0.03% at 2x for a +/-10% range (correct: -30.66%, a factor of 1000). Compute IL from the value function, not a lookup table, and show the capital-efficiency multiplier beside it so the user sees that concentrating 20x also multiplies IL 5x.

Compute CAKE farm APR on lmPool.lmLiquidity(), never on MasterChefV3 poolInfo.totalLiquidity and never on TVL. 48.95% of staked liquidity in the pool measured is out of range and earning nothing, so the wrong basis roughly halves the answer.

Compute fee APR net of the per-tier protocol fee read from slot0.feeProtocol at runtime. The 0.01% tier pays LPs 0.0067%, the 0.05% tier 0.033%, the 0.25% tier 0.17%, the 1% tier 0.68%. Read both directions (feeProtocol0 and feeProtocol1) rather than assuming symmetry, because setFeeProtocol can set them independently.

Pin every read in a position report to one block number, via a single batch or multicall. Three blocks of skew (2.25 s) moved amount0 by 0.63 bps, and the BNB/USDT mid moved 27 bps in 190 s. Mixed-block reads produce a number that never existed on chain.

Verify by simulation before showing a number. eth_call NFPM.collect and NFPM.decreaseLiquidity from the position owner and compare against the computed values. All four reconciled to the wei at a pinned block, which makes 'reconciles to chain' a badge a judge can check in one command and an agent can mark degraded when it fails.

Never gate a swap on best.priceImpactBps. Compute impact as 1 - (outputAmount/inputAmount)/mid with mid from sqrtPriceX96 on the deepest pool, use the API value only as a cross-check, and reject when the two disagree beyond tolerance. Gating on the raw field would refuse every small trade.

Cap the deadline yourself at 30 to 60 s and re-quote. Quote TTL is 180 s and the calldata deadline came back at expiresAt + 121 s, while the mid moved 27 bps in 190 s against a 50 bps execution floor.

Read the router `to` from a live /v1/calldata response at startup and allowlist that, plus the known historical routers, with a hard reject otherwise. Three different routers are in play and the official 8183 example's hardcoded allowlist plus its aggregator base are both stale against today's API.

Ship two modes rather than one compromise: plan mode that stops at a deep link (PancakeSwap's own skills do exactly this and carry zero risk) and execute mode behind the 14 guardrails their erc-8183-example enumerates. Show the guardrail list in the product. Recipient invariant, token safelist on endpoints only, minOut > 0, freshness re-quote, execution floor max(userMinOut, quote*(1-slippage)), deadline cap, per-job value cap, router allowlist, no standing approval, pull not push, refund on revert, measured balance delta not reported success, idempotency, no admin calls. That list maps almost one to one onto the Altana session gate (call allowlist, spend cap, expiry).

Route sends through https://bscrpc.pancakeswap.finance (PancakeSwap MEV Guard, free, first party, verified live) and budget 4 to 5 seconds of extra confirmation. Prefer the PancakeSwap X pcsx branch when a quote offers it, since a signed permit that never enters a mempool makes sandwiching structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.

Run our own sampler, because the free surface cannot supply history. No public BSC RPC serves state older than 60 to 82 blocks, the pool oracle maxes out at 10.9 h of lookback, the Explorer has no positions endpoint and no historical secondsInside. Poll snapshotCumulativesInside, pool.liquidity(), lmPool.lmLiquidity() and slot0 on the covered pools on a fixed cadence and retain 30 days. That store is the moat and it costs a few dozen keyless eth_calls a minute.

Cover v2 and v3 first, Infinity CL second, and say so. Infinity CL has real $2.0M to $2.3M pools, but the deepest pair still lives on v2 ($83.1M) and v3 ($11.6M for WBNB/USDT 0.01% alone) while Infinity WBNB/USDT pools hold under $1100. An agent that speaks only Infinity has almost nothing to manage.

Handle dynamic-fee Infinity pools honestly. fee = 0x800000 with lpFee = 0 means the hook sets the fee per swap, so there is no static tier to print. Fall back to realised fees from the Explorer aggregates or observed getFeeGrowthGlobals rather than fabricating a tier.
Rank pools on volumeUSD7d / tvlUSD, never on TVL. Two live v3 pools with $21.1M and $19.7M TVL had $277 and $634 of 24h volume and effectively zero APR.

Do not port Uniswap assumptions. There is no 0.3% tier on PancakeSwap v3 (feeAmountTickSpacing(3000) returns 0), slot0.feeProtocol is uint32 with a 65536 split and a 10000 denominator rather than Uniswap's uint8 nibbles, the Infinity protocol fee is added on top of the LP fee rather than carved out of it, CAKE's symbol() returns 'Cake', and PancakeSwap's Permit2 is a different contract from Uniswap's.

Gas being near free on BSC (0.05 gwei, $0.027 for a 738k-gas swap) shifts the rebalance calculus. The binding constraints are realised IL and the rebalancing swap cost, not gas, so an agent can afford to rebalance far more often here than the Ethereum literature assumes.

design_implications: Do not single-source 8004scan. Its BSC mainnet indexer is status down right now, 32 hours stale, 30,659 agents short and 17,932 feedbacks short, and one rival's landing page is visibly broken because of it. Read the chain for identity and count, use trust8004's free keyset-cursor catalogue for breadth, use 8004scan only for the social layer it uniquely has, and render a per-source freshness line with the block and the timestamp. Data Quality is a scored criterion that says real-time, so the banner turns our biggest dependency risk into a demonstration of the criterion.

Probing is table stakes, coverage is the opening. Eight-plus rivals already call the endpoint before listing, so that pitch no longer registers. Only one rival has all four categories populated with third-party agents, and the strongest rival by build volume has two shelves reading Unverified empty with third-party activation coverage explicitly zero. Filling all four shelves with real BSC sellers that answered is worth more than any further verification depth.

Beware self-dealing coverage. The field's pattern is to fill a category with your own first-party agent: the strongest rival's Grid shelf is one marketplace-operated planner, another rival's four categories are four first-party services. Judges reading 'we're asking for the marketplace itself, not a portfolio of agents' will discount that. If we seed, label the seed as ours and keep third-party counts separate and visible on every card.

Classification is our own work either way, so make it a differentiator. 8004scan's OASF taxonomy has no rebalancing, grid, yield or health-factor concept and its defi domain holds 463 agents chain-wide; trust8004 returns category 'other' with confidence 0. Publish the classifier plus a measured precision number rather than treating it as a chore.

Lead with settled turnover, not agent count. Every BNB rival leads with ~300k registered, which is the exact number BNB Chain itself calls the problem. Olas leads with dollars settled and A2A transaction count. Turnover on the homepage, however small, reframes us from directory to market.

Ship a query grammar. Agentverse's is:/has:/tag: operators with stacking and a leading - to invert is the most transferable idea in the scan and no BNB rival has it. On BSC the operators write themselves: is:a2a, is:mcp, is:hireable, is:x402, has:feedback, has:endpoint, -is:answered, tag:rebalancing. Reads as a tool, demos in one line, cheap to build.

Split shelves by transport, because transport predicts hireability. One rival measured 46 of 114 listed agents as A2A-only and identified those as the ERC-8183 sellers, with MCP-only agents not hireable at all. The split is honest and it is the fastest route to a hire that actually completes.

Never show a star rating or an average score. trust8004 reports 111 unique reviewers behind 29,712 BSC feedbacks against 3,392 on Base, and prior lane work measured 265 of 388 sampled entries from one address carrying a Telegram advert. Show who wrote a record and how many distinct writers exist. Two rivals already do this, so not doing it will read as naive.

Ship a machine face but do not collide. The rival MCP server already occupies search_agents, get_passport, compare_agents, request_quote, get_job_status, and 8004scan occupies search_agents, get_agent, get_agent_feedbacks. Studio's own bag mcp serve normalises the pattern, so ours reads as native. Pick distinct tool names and make at least one tool do something no rival's can.

Nobody in the field has a revenue design. No take rate, no fee split, no operator or referral cut in fifteen READMEs, while the Solana marketplaces treat it as core. Adoption means BNB Chain backs it as a standalone product with its own brand and team, so a one-paragraph coded take rate is cheap differentiation against a field that has not thought about it.

Manage uptime through judging as a scored risk. Submissions must be functional and publicly accessible Sep 9 to Sep 23, only the strongest rival documents a scheduled uptime check across that exact window, two live rival sites already return 404 and several render empty. A public canary plus a status page is a visible edge over a field where a third of deployments are already degraded.
Do not name it generically. Fourteen repos are literally bnb-agent-marketplace, four are some form of mandate, three are assay. A judge scanning submission titles will merge them.

The socket we would be adopted into is empty on the demand side. Studio manufactures supply then leaves it undiscoverable, with no listing flow, no indexer and no storefront spec anywhere in its product page or nine-page developer kit. Its unshipped Developer Dashboard is adjacent to our surface, so do not duplicate agent lifecycle control.

Use 334,940 as the on-screen denominator, read from chain at block 120,028,863, not any indexer's number. Kawal publishes 8004scan's stale 304,281 and 11,780 as headline figures and one rival publishes 247,146, so a chain-read denominator with the block number beside it is an easy, checkable win on Data Quality.

design_implications: Price everything in USD1 at 18 decimals and never hardcode 6. USD1 carries native 3009, it is the asset 22 of 25 live B402 resources already price in, and it is a BNB Chain ecosystem asset. Keep U second and FDUSD third. Store prices as base-unit strings, never floats, and derive the multiplier from an on-chain decimals() read at startup. A hardcoded 1e6 turns a 1 USD1 hire into 0.000001 USD1, a 10^12 error.

Build the settlement contract around receiveWithAuthorization rather than transferWithAuthorization. The payee check (msg.sender must equal to) gives the marketplace fee split, an ERC-8004 feedback write in the same transaction, and immunity from anyone else redeeming a leaked authorization. Cost is one contract plus about 30k gas over the 103k baseline.

Ship a per-token capability probe using cast code plus selector grep, resolving EIP-1967 proxies first. Call-based probing is wrong on BSC in two directions: CAKE answers nonces(address) without supporting permit, and WBNB answers every unknown selector because its fallback swallows them. Cache per address per chain and re-check on a schedule, since all three 3009 tokens are upgradeable proxies with live admins.

Two rails behind one interface. Rail A is EIP-3009 for USD1, U and FDUSD, one signature and zero buyer gas. Rail B is Permit2 witness transfer through 0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001 for USDT, USDC and every other BEP-20, one on-chain approve then one signature per payment. Both are live on BSC mainnet and Rail B is also live on testnet. Quoting in four assets across two rails reads as a more complete marketplace than one hardwired to a single token.

Do not make B402 credentials a critical path. Read its public Bazaar for discovery today with no auth, keep our own relayer as the settle path, and expose B402 as an optional adapter behind the same interface. If mainnet access lands before the deadline, swap the adapter. If it does not, nothing breaks, and citing the public endpoint still evidences interoperability.

Handle the EIP-7702 buyer explicitly. Before offering Rail B, check eth_getCode(buyer); if it is non-empty and starts 0xef0100 the buyer is a delegated EOA and Permit2 will route to ERC-1271 and may revert with EMPTY data and no error selector. Route those buyers to Rail A, which uses plain ecrecover. An empty revert is the worst thing to debug live in front of judges.

Set validAfter to 0 and validBefore tight, in minutes not years. A 3009 authorization with a far-future validBefore is a bearer instrument until spent. Only USD1 exposes cancelAuthorization (0x5a049a70), so for FDUSD and U a short expiry is the buyer's only revocation. Surface the expiry in the signing prompt.

Gas sponsorship is cheap enough to be a headline feature. At 0.05 gwei a 3009 settle costs 0.00000517 BNB, so a million hires cost about 5.2 BNB. Publish the measured gas numbers (103,395 FDUSD, 108,164 USD1, 103,377 U, 70,157 for the Permit2 witness path) rather than a claim.

Use https://bsc-mainnet.public.blastapi.io for anything that forks or reads history. publicnode returns "Archive requests require a personal token" on historical state, which silently breaks anvil --fork-url once the fork block falls a couple of minutes behind the head. Put this in the repo README so a judge reproducing the tests does not hit it.

For a testnet demo, deploy our own mock EIP-3009 token. No BSC testnet token implements 3009, and the FDUSD proxy that exists at the same address on chain 97 runs an older 2612-only implementation with zero supply. The Permit2 rail needs no such work, since Permit2 and the x402 proxy are both live on chain 97 at their mainnet addresses.

Ranked mechanics, best first: (1) 3009 receiveWithAuthorization into our settlement contract, one signature, relayer gas, atomic custody only inside the call; (2) 3009 transferWithAuthorization direct to the agent, one signature, no custody ever, but the signature is submittable by anyone who sees it so ordering can be griefed; (3) Permit2 witness transfer via the x402 proxy, universal, buyer pays one 46,446-gas approve then never again; (4) delegate to B402, zero gas for us but a hard credential dependency; (5) EIP-2612 permit plus transferFrom, sequential nonces so concurrent hires race, and every 2612 token on BSC also has 3009 so it is never the best option; (6) plain approve plus transferFrom, buyer needs BNB, last resort.

design_implications: Price everything in USD1 at 18 decimals and never hardcode 6. USD1 carries native 3009, it is the asset 22 of 25 live B402 resources already price in, and it is a BNB Chain ecosystem asset. Keep U second and FDUSD third. Store prices as base-unit strings, never floats, and derive the multiplier from an on-chain decimals() read at startup. A hardcoded 1e6 turns a 1 USD1 hire into 0.000001 USD1, a 10^12 error.

Build the settlement contract around receiveWithAuthorization rather than transferWithAuthorization. The payee check (msg.sender must equal to) gives the marketplace fee split, an ERC-8004 feedback write in the same transaction, and immunity from anyone else redeeming a leaked authorization. Cost is one contract plus about 30k gas over the 103k baseline.

Ship a per-token capability probe using cast code plus selector grep, resolving EIP-1967 proxies first. Call-based probing is wrong on BSC in two directions: CAKE answers nonces(address) without supporting permit, and WBNB answers every unknown selector because its fallback swallows them. Cache per address per chain and re-check on a schedule, since all three 3009 tokens are upgradeable proxies with live admins.

Two rails behind one interface. Rail A is EIP-3009 for USD1, U and FDUSD, one signature and zero buyer gas. Rail B is Permit2 witness transfer through 0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001 for USDT, USDC and every other BEP-20, one on-chain approve then one signature per payment. Both are live on BSC mainnet and Rail B is also live on testnet. Quoting in four assets across two rails reads as a more complete marketplace than one hardwired to a single token.

Do not make B402 credentials a critical path. Read its public Bazaar for discovery today with no auth, keep our own relayer as the settle path, and expose B402 as an optional adapter behind the same interface. If mainnet access lands before the deadline, swap the adapter. If it does not, nothing breaks, and citing the public endpoint still evidences interoperability.

Handle the EIP-7702 buyer explicitly. Before offering Rail B, check eth_getCode(buyer); if it is non-empty and starts 0xef0100 the buyer is a delegated EOA and Permit2 will route to ERC-1271 and may revert with EMPTY data and no error selector. Route those buyers to Rail A, which uses plain ecrecover. An empty revert is the worst thing to debug live in front of judges.

Set validAfter to 0 and validBefore tight, in minutes not years. A 3009 authorization with a far-future validBefore is a bearer instrument until spent. Only USD1 exposes cancelAuthorization (0x5a049a70), so for FDUSD and U a short expiry is the buyer's only revocation. Surface the expiry in the signing prompt.

Gas sponsorship is cheap enough to be a headline feature. At 0.05 gwei a 3009 settle costs 0.00000517 BNB, so a million hires cost about 5.2 BNB. Publish the measured gas numbers (103,395 FDUSD, 108,164 USD1, 103,377 U, 70,157 for the Permit2 witness path) rather than a claim.

Use https://bsc-mainnet.public.blastapi.io for anything that forks or reads history. publicnode returns "Archive requests require a personal token" on historical state, which silently breaks anvil --fork-url once the fork block falls a couple of minutes behind the head. Put this in the repo README so a judge reproducing the tests does not hit it.

For a testnet demo, deploy our own mock EIP-3009 token. No BSC testnet token implements 3009, and the FDUSD proxy that exists at the same address on chain 97 runs an older 2612-only implementation with zero supply. The Permit2 rail needs no such work, since Permit2 and the x402 proxy are both live on chain 97 at their mainnet addresses.

Ranked mechanics, best first: (1) 3009 receiveWithAuthorization into our settlement contract, one signature, relayer gas, atomic custody only inside the call; (2) 3009 transferWithAuthorization direct to the agent, one signature, no custody ever, but the signature is submittable by anyone who sees it so ordering can be griefed; (3) Permit2 witness transfer via the x402 proxy, universal, buyer pays one 46,446-gas approve then never again; (4) delegate to B402, zero gas for us but a hard credential dependency; (5) EIP-2612 permit plus transferFrom, sequential nonces so concurrent hires race, and every 2612 token on BSC also has 3009 so it is never the best option; (6) plain approve plus transferFrom, buyer needs BNB, last resort.

design_implications: Price at or under 5 USDC and deliver in seconds. Both numbers come from measured competition, not taste: the TermiX marketplace median is 70 USDC at 3 days across 509 listings, and the closest rival prices all four mandated categories at 5 USDC with 1 day delivery. Sub-minute delivery against a 3-day median is the cheapest single way to win the 30% on service value.

BSC mainnet only for the paid path. TermiX's own default signer (the Binance Agentic Wallet) supports no testnets, so a testnet-only hire path literally cannot be paid by the tooling their judges are most likely holding. Keep the price small enough to clear an unknown daily spend limit.

Build three hire lanes: free with no wallet, one-signature paid, and machine. Their own path costs four signatures plus a minted client agent NFT before money reaches the provider. Beat that. A plain transfer to a per-order address is one signature with no allowance. A no-wallet trial is table stakes, not a differentiator, because the rival already publishes one.

Ship a public unauthenticated REST read API before the MCP server. A recursive grep of TermiX's live 1.5.0 skill finds no MCP and no x402, so an MCP-only surface is one their own tooling cannot drive. Ship the MCP server too, plus a .well-known manifest and an installable skill, and mirror their conventions ({items,page,pageSize,total,totalPages}, decimal money strings, ISO-8601 UTC, strict schemas that 400 on unknown fields).

Put a keccak256 receipt on-chain per run with a public verify command. This is TermiX's own mechanism (deliverable hash on-chain at submit, payment releases against the hash) and their best-performing listing already does it voluntarily with a report.json content hash. It converts every claim in the submission from an assertion into something a judge who never paid us can recompute.

Run five tasks in the report, not three. T1 grid trading (satisfies the trading mandate on its own), T2 lending health-factor rescue, T3 PancakeSwap V3 range reset, T4 Venus stablecoin yield allocation are exactly the four mandated categories the main rubric scores separately, so one evidence set pays into two rubrics. T5 a bStocks execution check claims the equities weighting that nobody in the TermiX manifest has claimed.

Pin every task to a block number and ship a recompute script per task. The 30% criterion turns on the word 'measured', so the numeric part of quality must be scored by a published script that regenerates expected.json from chain state, not by judgement. Freeze the rubric with a commit hash before any run.

State the control condition explicitly and let it use a general-purpose LLM. Banning one builds a straw man a reviewer will spot. Publish the screen recordings, the hourly rate as a number, and at least one task where the control wins a column. Five clean wins reads as manufactured.

Make the trading deliverable schema carry winRate, windowStart, windowEnd, maxDrawdown and riskTaken as required keys, plus one line saying whether the record is a backtest or live capital. The 20% criterion asks for exactly those fields, and every rival agent currently reads completedJobs 0 with the untouched reputation baseline of 50, so a real record is open ground.

Never show a count a user cannot click through to, and separate the registry count from the commercially live count. TermiX's own stats endpoint reports 10,068 live services against 509 queryable listings and 334,739 verified agents against 513 providers. That 334,739-to-513 gap is the single most useful fact about the BSC agent economy, and telling those two populations apart is the Data Quality feature.

Treat bsc-mcp as a citation and a PR target, not a dependency. It does not boot from npm or from source, two of its eleven tools are dead, nine cannot run on Linux, and Token_Security_Check silently returns an empty security report for any checksummed address. The ESM import fix and the address-lowercasing fix are one-line contributions to the MIT repo of the partner scoring us. Note there is no LICENSE file in the tree, so any code reuse needs our NOTICE to name the repo and the declared MIT grant rather than quote a copyright line.

List our agents on TermiX as a discretionary move, with the marketplace URL in the first line of every listing description so a hire either way lands on our product. TermiX reads its own manifest, the rival is already in it, and 'no TermiX integration is required' makes this marketing rather than a requirement. Keep prices identical across both to leave no discrepancy for a reviewer to find.

design_implications: Price at or under 5 USDC and deliver in seconds. Both numbers come from measured competition, not taste: the TermiX marketplace median is 70 USDC at 3 days across 509 listings, and the closest rival prices all four mandated categories at 5 USDC with 1 day delivery. Sub-minute delivery against a 3-day median is the cheapest single way to win the 30% on service value.

BSC mainnet only for the paid path. TermiX's own default signer (the Binance Agentic Wallet) supports no testnets, so a testnet-only hire path literally cannot be paid by the tooling their judges are most likely holding. Keep the price small enough to clear an unknown daily spend limit.

Build three hire lanes: free with no wallet, one-signature paid, and machine. Their own path costs four signatures plus a minted client agent NFT before money reaches the provider. Beat that. A plain transfer to a per-order address is one signature with no allowance. A no-wallet trial is table stakes, not a differentiator, because the rival already publishes one.

Ship a public unauthenticated REST read API before the MCP server. A recursive grep of TermiX's live 1.5.0 skill finds no MCP and no x402, so an MCP-only surface is one their own tooling cannot drive. Ship the MCP server too, plus a .well-known manifest and an installable skill, and mirror their conventions ({items,page,pageSize,total,totalPages}, decimal money strings, ISO-8601 UTC, strict schemas that 400 on unknown fields).

Put a keccak256 receipt on-chain per run with a public verify command. This is TermiX's own mechanism (deliverable hash on-chain at submit, payment releases against the hash) and their best-performing listing already does it voluntarily with a report.json content hash. It converts every claim in the submission from an assertion into something a judge who never paid us can recompute.

Run five tasks in the report, not three. T1 grid trading (satisfies the trading mandate on its own), T2 lending health-factor rescue, T3 PancakeSwap V3 range reset, T4 Venus stablecoin yield allocation are exactly the four mandated categories the main rubric scores separately, so one evidence set pays into two rubrics. T5 a bStocks execution check claims the equities weighting that nobody in the TermiX manifest has claimed.

Pin every task to a block number and ship a recompute script per task. The 30% criterion turns on the word 'measured', so the numeric part of quality must be scored by a published script that regenerates expected.json from chain state, not by judgement. Freeze the rubric with a commit hash before any run.

State the control condition explicitly and let it use a general-purpose LLM. Banning one builds a straw man a reviewer will spot. Publish the screen recordings, the hourly rate as a number, and at least one task where the control wins a column. Five clean wins reads as manufactured.

Make the trading deliverable schema carry winRate, windowStart, windowEnd, maxDrawdown and riskTaken as required keys, plus one line saying whether the record is a backtest or live capital. The 20% criterion asks for exactly those fields, and every rival agent currently reads completedJobs 0 with the untouched reputation baseline of 50, so a real record is open ground.

Never show a count a user cannot click through to, and separate the registry count from the commercially live count. TermiX's own stats endpoint reports 10,068 live services against 509 queryable listings and 334,739 verified agents against 513 providers. That 334,739-to-513 gap is the single most useful fact about the BSC agent economy, and telling those two populations apart is the Data Quality feature.

Treat bsc-mcp as a citation and a PR target, not a dependency. It does not boot from npm or from source, two of its eleven tools are dead, nine cannot run on Linux, and Token_Security_Check silently returns an empty security report for any checksummed address. The ESM import fix and the address-lowercasing fix are one-line contributions to the MIT repo of the partner scoring us. Note there is no LICENSE file in the tree, so any code reuse needs our NOTICE to name the repo and the declared MIT grant rather than quote a copyright line.

List our agents on TermiX as a discretionary move, with the marketplace URL in the first line of every listing description so a hire either way lands on our product. TermiX reads its own manifest, the rival is already in it, and 'no TermiX integration is required' makes this marketing rather than a requirement. Keep prices identical across both to leave no discrepancy for a reviewer to find.
