design_implications: Build the G5 permission panel as four live eth_calls, not cached state: canExecutePackedInfos(keyHash) for the allowlist, spendInfos(keyHash) for the caps, getExpiry(wallet,keyId) for the countdown, isValidKey(wallet,keyId) for live-versus-revoked. The judge can run the identical calls and get the identical answer, so the product IS the evidence. A cached panel reads as a pitch.

Ship on BSC mainnet, not testnet. The requirement says mainnet is stronger and the cost is 0.000694 BNB per key registration ($0.50, Chainlink-priced) plus gas: four agents with one session each is eight registrations, under $5 total against $30,000 plus 50,000 XP.

Mainnet has only 123 keys ever registered and 56 live, so eight registrations move the whole registry ~6% and will likely appear on the explorer's front-page activity feed (paginated 25 at a time across 157 events). Time the grants for the days after submission rather than weeks before.

Show both key identifiers with their derivations: keyId = keccak256(SEC1 pubkey) for the Keystore, keyHash = keccak256(abi.encode(uint8 keyType, keccak256(publicKeyBytes))) for the account. Conflating them is the most likely integration bug in the track and showing both signals we read the contracts.

Health factor is the one mandated category the skills registry does not cover (Venus is supply-only, the Aave skill's display.mayNot literally lists "Borrow"), so build it straight from getUserAccountData on the Aave Pool and getAccountLiquidity plus markets on the Venus Comptroller. Every rival assembling four agents out of the ten published skills will be weakest in exactly the category the rubric mandates.

The four categories collapse into two session shapes: rebalancing and grid trading both need approve on a basket plus the PancakeSwap V2 router under a daily cap; yield needs approve plus two or three methods on one protocol; health factor needs approve plus repay and supply. Four narrow scopes score better on Altana's rubric than one wide session and look less lazy on the main rubric.

Never omit permissions.calls. It grants every target inside the spend cap, which fails G2 on inspection even though the cap is real. Never scope the ERC-8004 registry with {to: registry} either: that also authorizes transferFrom, setApprovalForAll and setAgentWallet.
Never grant with register: false on anything we submit. It saves $0.50 and voids G3, because an unregistered session is invisible to verify_authorization and to the explorer.

Set stablecoin caps at 18 decimals. USDT and USDC are 18 on BNB Chain and 6 on Ethereum, so 100_000_000n on BSC is a cap of 0.0000000001 USDT and the agent reverts against a limit that reads generous.

Always pass our own sessionSigner and persist with serializeSession plus a separate secret store. An SDK-generated key lives only in process memory, and losing it strands a live on-chain authorization with revoke-and-regrant as the only exit. Never JSON.stringify a Session.

Do not rely on the SDK's fundNative for tBNB: on the testnet relay today it encodes mint(address,uint256) against the zero address and no-ops. Use https://testnet.bnbchain.org/faucet-smart, and for $U use requestTokens() on 0x86e9197CC0F76E4e4aaa7082180945196bBAb5D3 (10 $U per 30 minutes).

Both bonuses are shipped SDK APIs so both are cheap: hireErc8183Agent for the buyer side and submitErc8183Deliverable plus erc8183SubmitPermissions for the seller side, and one @altananetwork/x402-server guarded route offering both rails (eip3009 $U for Studio buyers, permit2-exact USDT) with maxTimeoutSeconds <= 480 or Studio's signer refuses.

Split the hire demo across networks: the ERC-8183 dispute window is 7 days on mainnet and 1 day on testnet, so a mainnet hire started late cannot settle inside judging week. Run the full loop on testnet, the DeFi agents on mainnet, or start the mainnet job at submission and show claimRefund plus dispute as user-controlled branches.

Drive the consent screen off the registry's own fields: display.may / display.mayNot is plain-English permission copy the protocol publisher already wrote, and inputs[].askAt is "grant" or "run", which is the consent-screen versus run-screen split handed to us. scope.contracts is prose, so the real addresses have to come from the SKILL.md address tables.

Link the explorer as third-party evidence but read the contract for anything the UI asserts. On 2026-09-05 an account page reported 0 keys while getKeys returned 2, and a key page fell back to indexed history because the live node read was unavailable.
Budget a paid RPC for any indexing: publicnode 403s on archive reads and cast logs over the Keystore timed out at 120s on three public endpoints. Live view calls are fine on the free nodes.

Publish one skill to https://skills.altana.network/submit, ideally the health-factor gap. Altana fork-tests before listing, so it is real upstream work that stands on its own and is a durable third-party endorsement of the entry.

Grab the free 3,000 XP by doing the three quests (create, fund, grant) on the wallets we submit. They are steps 1 to 3 of the build anyway, and every agent wallet needs native BNB because the relay reports only the native token as a fee token on every chain.
Keep sessions' expiries past 2026-09-23. Judging runs Sep 9 to 23 and an expired session shows as a dead agent, plus the marketplace must stay publicly reachable for the whole window.
Pin the SDK to 0.9.0 (published 2026-09-02) and note that porto is pinned exactly to 0.2.37. Read source from the staging branch, not main, since staging is the repo default and main lags.

design_implications: Build the G5 permission panel as four live eth_calls, not cached state: canExecutePackedInfos(keyHash) for the allowlist, spendInfos(keyHash) for the caps, getExpiry(wallet,keyId) for the countdown, isValidKey(wallet,keyId) for live-versus-revoked. The judge can run the identical calls and get the identical answer, so the product IS the evidence. A cached panel reads as a pitch.

Ship on BSC mainnet, not testnet. The requirement says mainnet is stronger and the cost is 0.000694 BNB per key registration ($0.50, Chainlink-priced) plus gas: four agents with one session each is eight registrations, under $5 total against $30,000 plus 50,000 XP.

Mainnet has only 123 keys ever registered and 56 live, so eight registrations move the whole registry ~6% and will likely appear on the explorer's front-page activity feed (paginated 25 at a time across 157 events). Time the grants for the days after submission rather than weeks before.

Show both key identifiers with their derivations: keyId = keccak256(SEC1 pubkey) for the Keystore, keyHash = keccak256(abi.encode(uint8 keyType, keccak256(publicKeyBytes))) for the account. Conflating them is the most likely integration bug in the track and showing both signals we read the contracts.

Health factor is the one mandated category the skills registry does not cover (Venus is supply-only, the Aave skill's display.mayNot literally lists "Borrow"), so build it straight from getUserAccountData on the Aave Pool and getAccountLiquidity plus markets on the Venus Comptroller. Every rival assembling four agents out of the ten published skills will be weakest in exactly the category the rubric mandates.

The four categories collapse into two session shapes: rebalancing and grid trading both need approve on a basket plus the PancakeSwap V2 router under a daily cap; yield needs approve plus two or three methods on one protocol; health factor needs approve plus repay and supply. Four narrow scopes score better on Altana's rubric than one wide session and look less lazy on the main rubric.

Never omit permissions.calls. It grants every target inside the spend cap, which fails G2 on inspection even though the cap is real. Never scope the ERC-8004 registry with {to: registry} either: that also authorizes transferFrom, setApprovalForAll and setAgentWallet.
Never grant with register: false on anything we submit. It saves $0.50 and voids G3, because an unregistered session is invisible to verify_authorization and to the explorer.

Set stablecoin caps at 18 decimals. USDT and USDC are 18 on BNB Chain and 6 on Ethereum, so 100_000_000n on BSC is a cap of 0.0000000001 USDT and the agent reverts against a limit that reads generous.

Always pass our own sessionSigner and persist with serializeSession plus a separate secret store. An SDK-generated key lives only in process memory, and losing it strands a live on-chain authorization with revoke-and-regrant as the only exit. Never JSON.stringify a Session.

Do not rely on the SDK's fundNative for tBNB: on the testnet relay today it encodes mint(address,uint256) against the zero address and no-ops. Use https://testnet.bnbchain.org/faucet-smart, and for $U use requestTokens() on 0x86e9197CC0F76E4e4aaa7082180945196bBAb5D3 (10 $U per 30 minutes).

Both bonuses are shipped SDK APIs so both are cheap: hireErc8183Agent for the buyer side and submitErc8183Deliverable plus erc8183SubmitPermissions for the seller side, and one @altananetwork/x402-server guarded route offering both rails (eip3009 $U for Studio buyers, permit2-exact USDT) with maxTimeoutSeconds <= 480 or Studio's signer refuses.

Split the hire demo across networks: the ERC-8183 dispute window is 7 days on mainnet and 1 day on testnet, so a mainnet hire started late cannot settle inside judging week. Run the full loop on testnet, the DeFi agents on mainnet, or start the mainnet job at submission and show claimRefund plus dispute as user-controlled branches.

Drive the consent screen off the registry's own fields: display.may / display.mayNot is plain-English permission copy the protocol publisher already wrote, and inputs[].askAt is "grant" or "run", which is the consent-screen versus run-screen split handed to us. scope.contracts is prose, so the real addresses have to come from the SKILL.md address tables.

Link the explorer as third-party evidence but read the contract for anything the UI asserts. On 2026-09-05 an account page reported 0 keys while getKeys returned 2, and a key page fell back to indexed history because the live node read was unavailable.
Budget a paid RPC for any indexing: publicnode 403s on archive reads and cast logs over the Keystore timed out at 120s on three public endpoints. Live view calls are fine on the free nodes.

Publish one skill to https://skills.altana.network/submit, ideally the health-factor gap. Altana fork-tests before listing, so it is real upstream work that stands on its own and is a durable third-party endorsement of the entry.

Grab the free 3,000 XP by doing the three quests (create, fund, grant) on the wallets we submit. They are steps 1 to 3 of the build anyway, and every agent wallet needs native BNB because the relay reports only the native token as a fee token on every chain.
Keep sessions' expiries past 2026-09-23. Judging runs Sep 9 to 23 and an expired session shows as a dead agent, plus the marketplace must stay publicly reachable for the whole window.
Pin the SDK to 0.9.0 (published 2026-09-02) and note that porto is pinned exactly to 0.2.37. Read source from the staging branch, not main, since staging is the repo default and main lags.

design_implications: BABT must be a TIER, never a GATE. 1.0% of BSC agent owners hold one (6 of 585 measured), so a hard requirement to list deletes 99% of the catalogue and destroys the Agent Diversity score, which is one of the three named rubric criteria. A gated marketplace would have roughly nine listable agents out of a 600-agent pool and could not fill four mandated categories.

Ship a five-rung ladder where each rung is one balanceOf or one aggregate3 slot: Tier 0 Listed (an ERC-8004 agent id whose agentWallet matches the signer, ranked last, provisional review score), Tier 1 Bonded (refundable stake in our escrow, permissionless, no KYC, main list plus dispute eligibility), Tier 2 Proven (N settled x402/B402 payments as seller plus real on-chain trade history in its own category, unlocks the four category tabs and full review weight), Tier 3 Attested (BABT OR Galxe Passport OR a BNB Passport user_finished_one_of_attestation hit, unlocks the human-verified badge, higher caps, first page, dispute filing), Tier 4 Accountable (Tier 3 plus an Altana Keystore session with a readable and revocable allowlist, cap and expiry, unlocks ERC-8183 hiring and top of default sort).

Tier 3 must be an OR, not an AND. That is the whole answer to exclusion. BABT needs a Binance account; Galxe Passport needs Sumsub and no exchange at all; the BNB Passport SDK documents kyc_binance, kyc_bithumb, kyc_upbit, kyc_coinbase, kyc_okx and kyc_bybit, which covers Korea and the US where a Binance account may be unavailable. Tier 1 (a bond) must never require Tier 3, because a bond is the only rung a pseudonymous or restricted-jurisdiction operator can always reach.

Gate the REVIEW WRITE PATH, not the listing, because that is where an attestation is nearly free. 31 addresses wrote the last 3,000 BSC feedbacks, the top 10 wrote 65.3%, and none of the top 12 holds any attestation. giveFeedback has no authorisation beyond a one-wallet-deep self-feedback check, so it costs nothing but gas today.

Bind full-weight reviews to a settled payment. The x402/B402 settle response returns {success, payer, transaction, network}, so make that payer the only address allowed to review that agent for that transaction, once. Proof of purchase makes a sybil pay real money per review instead of gas.

Cap displayed feedback at one per author per agent (one address left 12 on a single agent on chain) and show each author's distinct-agent count beside their review, so a 35-agent reviewer is visibly a bot. Compute and display OUR reweighted score as ours, link the raw 8004 number, and never present the raw number as truth: doing so imports the farm wholesale.
Do not render appendResponse output as the agent's official reply unless msg.sender equals the agent owner. The function has no ownership check at all, so anyone can append to anyone's feedback.

Keep the check stateless. Read at request time, cache the READ for about 60 seconds keyed by address, and never persist a durable verified: true flag: 11.58% of all BABTs ever minted are already revoked or burned and the issuer can revoke unilaterally.

Never store the metadata id and never store the tokenId. The id is the stable per-person identifier, so persisting it builds the cross-wallet identity graph Binance deliberately made unbuildable by 404ing revoked tokens. The tokenId changes on re-mint and Binance says outright not to use it as a user key. There is no PII in a BABT to leak, only an identifier-correlation risk we create ourselves.

Word the UI honestly. "Holds a Binance Account Bound Token" is verifiable. "KYC verified by Binance" is not ours to say, because Binance states it makes no representation about holders and that its verification procedures vary by country of residence.

Treat BABT as ISBT721, never as ERC-721. supportsInterface(0x80ac58cd) returns true while transferFrom does not exist, and the reverts carry no revert data at all, so interface sniffing plus a reason-string UI both fail silently. Use balanceOf in gates because tokenIdOf reverts for non-holders and would bubble up and kill the transaction.

Batch the whole ladder in one round trip through Multicall3 aggregate3 at 0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11, mixing BABT balanceOf, Galxe Passport balanceOf and BNB Passport user_finished_one_of_attestation in a single call array. Verified working on BSC.

Record {address, tier, blockNumber, timestamp} alongside each review at write time, because historical eth_call is 403 on free public RPCs, so a later replay of "was this address verified then" is impossible. Storing the result rather than replaying the check is auditable and stores no identity.

Make the whole verification story reproducible in the repo: every claim in this pass is a one-line cast call against a public RPC, so ship those exact lines in a script a judge can run that prints the block number with each result, plus a page-level count of how many listed agents are attested. That reads as Data Quality; a modal blocking 99% of the catalogue reads as a broken marketplace.

Use BSC testnet BABT at 0x984E6a7b9cb73cB7884c9ca9b1Ee625546F9D0E3 (chain 97) to exercise the gate in CI, but note its tokenURI resolves to IPFS rather than the bapi host, so do not assume the metadata shape matches mainnet, and testnet minting is request-only via a form.

design_implications: BABT must be a TIER, never a GATE. 1.0% of BSC agent owners hold one (6 of 585 measured), so a hard requirement to list deletes 99% of the catalogue and destroys the Agent Diversity score, which is one of the three named rubric criteria. A gated marketplace would have roughly nine listable agents out of a 600-agent pool and could not fill four mandated categories.

Ship a five-rung ladder where each rung is one balanceOf or one aggregate3 slot: Tier 0 Listed (an ERC-8004 agent id whose agentWallet matches the signer, ranked last, provisional review score), Tier 1 Bonded (refundable stake in our escrow, permissionless, no KYC, main list plus dispute eligibility), Tier 2 Proven (N settled x402/B402 payments as seller plus real on-chain trade history in its own category, unlocks the four category tabs and full review weight), Tier 3 Attested (BABT OR Galxe Passport OR a BNB Passport user_finished_one_of_attestation hit, unlocks the human-verified badge, higher caps, first page, dispute filing), Tier 4 Accountable (Tier 3 plus an Altana Keystore session with a readable and revocable allowlist, cap and expiry, unlocks ERC-8183 hiring and top of default sort).

Tier 3 must be an OR, not an AND. That is the whole answer to exclusion. BABT needs a Binance account; Galxe Passport needs Sumsub and no exchange at all; the BNB Passport SDK documents kyc_binance, kyc_bithumb, kyc_upbit, kyc_coinbase, kyc_okx and kyc_bybit, which covers Korea and the US where a Binance account may be unavailable. Tier 1 (a bond) must never require Tier 3, because a bond is the only rung a pseudonymous or restricted-jurisdiction operator can always reach.

Gate the REVIEW WRITE PATH, not the listing, because that is where an attestation is nearly free. 31 addresses wrote the last 3,000 BSC feedbacks, the top 10 wrote 65.3%, and none of the top 12 holds any attestation. giveFeedback has no authorisation beyond a one-wallet-deep self-feedback check, so it costs nothing but gas today.

Bind full-weight reviews to a settled payment. The x402/B402 settle response returns {success, payer, transaction, network}, so make that payer the only address allowed to review that agent for that transaction, once. Proof of purchase makes a sybil pay real money per review instead of gas.

Cap displayed feedback at one per author per agent (one address left 12 on a single agent on chain) and show each author's distinct-agent count beside their review, so a 35-agent reviewer is visibly a bot. Compute and display OUR reweighted score as ours, link the raw 8004 number, and never present the raw number as truth: doing so imports the farm wholesale.
Do not render appendResponse output as the agent's official reply unless msg.sender equals the agent owner. The function has no ownership check at all, so anyone can append to anyone's feedback.

Keep the check stateless. Read at request time, cache the READ for about 60 seconds keyed by address, and never persist a durable verified: true flag: 11.58% of all BABTs ever minted are already revoked or burned and the issuer can revoke unilaterally.

Never store the metadata id and never store the tokenId. The id is the stable per-person identifier, so persisting it builds the cross-wallet identity graph Binance deliberately made unbuildable by 404ing revoked tokens. The tokenId changes on re-mint and Binance says outright not to use it as a user key. There is no PII in a BABT to leak, only an identifier-correlation risk we create ourselves.

Word the UI honestly. "Holds a Binance Account Bound Token" is verifiable. "KYC verified by Binance" is not ours to say, because Binance states it makes no representation about holders and that its verification procedures vary by country of residence.

Treat BABT as ISBT721, never as ERC-721. supportsInterface(0x80ac58cd) returns true while transferFrom does not exist, and the reverts carry no revert data at all, so interface sniffing plus a reason-string UI both fail silently. Use balanceOf in gates because tokenIdOf reverts for non-holders and would bubble up and kill the transaction.

Batch the whole ladder in one round trip through Multicall3 aggregate3 at 0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11, mixing BABT balanceOf, Galxe Passport balanceOf and BNB Passport user_finished_one_of_attestation in a single call array. Verified working on BSC.

Record {address, tier, blockNumber, timestamp} alongside each review at write time, because historical eth_call is 403 on free public RPCs, so a later replay of "was this address verified then" is impossible. Storing the result rather than replaying the check is auditable and stores no identity.

Make the whole verification story reproducible in the repo: every claim in this pass is a one-line cast call against a public RPC, so ship those exact lines in a script a judge can run that prints the block number with each result, plus a page-level count of how many listed agents are attested. That reads as Data Quality; a modal blocking 99% of the catalogue reads as a broken marketplace.

Use BSC testnet BABT at 0x984E6a7b9cb73cB7884c9ca9b1Ee625546F9D0E3 (chain 97) to exercise the gate in CI, but note its tokenURI resolves to IPFS rather than the bapi host, so do not assume the metadata shape matches mainnet, and testnet minting is request-only via a form.

design_implications: Never take custody and never sit in the payment flow. The marketplace quotes, the buyer signs, the facilitator or an escrow whose keys we do not hold moves value, and the platform fee is a split inside that same settlement. This is the FIN-2019-G001 forum position, and running our own x402 facilitator that collects then remits crosses into the money-transmitter definition.

Screen on the quote path with four keyless calls and re-run at settlement: isSanctioned on 0x40C57923924B5c5c5455c48D93317139ADDaC8fb, membership of the locally ingested SDN EVM set with the chain tag ignored, frozen(payer) and frozen(payee), and paused() on the settlement token. Run all four on the buyer, the seller's payee and the agent's registered wallet, since setAgentWallet can change the payee independently.

One screening source is provably not enough. 20 of the 42 BSC-active SDN addresses are invisible to the oracle, and only one SDN address carries a BNB tag (and it is not even EVM-format), so ignore OFAC's chain tag entirely and screen the union of all 91 0x addresses plus the oracle.

Handle results asymmetrically. A direct-counterparty hit is a hard block, logged, with a reason shown. Graph proximity, an issuer freeze on an unrelated address, or a partial match is a review flag and never an automatic action, because inbound taint lets an attacker pick who gets frozen.

Refuse to quote when the escrow token is frozen or paused, before the user commits. Two extra eth_calls turn a mid-job failure into a clean pre-quote refusal, and they are the only visibility anyone has into the GENIUS Act freeze layer. Guard the calls, because BSC-USD implements neither.

Build every agent output as one of four shapes: measurement, comparison on published criteria, user-parameterised simulation, or mechanical execution of a user-set rule. That keeps the product outside the MiCA and MiFID II definition of advice by construction rather than by disclaimer. Show the downside beside the upside, and attach the block and source to every number.

Never claim independence. A marketplace takes a sell-side fee, which is a third-party benefit under MiCA Art 81(3)(b), so publish the fee and the ranking methodology and state that neither is advice, instead of asserting independence while taking a listing fee.

Present as a broker and behave like one: operator named on every listing and receipt, published ranking methodology, no outcome warranties, no first-party framing of third-party agents. DSA Art 6(3) removes the consumer-protection safe harbour exactly where a platform looks like the seller, and "official marketplace" framing plus heavy curation is that fact pattern.

Pin the keccak of the agent's reviewed metadata and card at review time and re-check on a schedule, treating drift as a new listing. setAgentURI, setMetadata and setAgentWallet are owner-callable at any time, so without this, "reviewed" has no referent.

Only count ERC-8004 feedback bound to a settled job with a distinct payer, show the settled-job count beside the score, label unbound feedback as unverified, and publish the rule. UCPD Annex I 23b and 23c make the alternative unfair in all circumstances, and this is simultaneously the honest answer to Data Quality on the rubric.

Collect nothing that creates the identification link. Wallet signature as the only account, no email, no IP joined to an address, no identity documents until an obligation attaches. The EDPB says an address becomes personal data when our own database can link it, and both DSA Art 10(2)(b) and 18 USC 2703(c)(2) only reach data already collected, so minimal collection is a compliance asset rather than a gap.

Keep nothing personal on-chain beyond what the transaction inherently carries: hashes and ids, never briefs or contents. EDPB Recommendation 11 says that if a technical deletion or anonymisation path does not exist then no personal data should go on the chain at all.

Emit a statement of reasons automatically from every enforcement action, with an onChainEffect field that reads "none", because the ERC-8004 registries are append-only and takedown means delisting from our index. The privacy notice and the takedown policy must say that in the same words.

Build both complaint systems, not one: DSA Art 20 for buyers (electronic, free, six-month window, reversal path) and P2B Art 11 for sellers, plus a public page rendering the four Art 11(4) statistics. TermiX, the incumbent in the sponsor track, publishes no terms at all, so clearing this bar is cheap and visible.

Split the licence by entry versus contribution: SAND-1.0 on the marketplace app and the ranking implementation (the judged, forkable surface), Apache-2.0 on the compliance layer and the four reference agents (the pieces meant to be adopted), CC0 on any published schema, and a separate ADOPTION.md rather than a pre-assignment, since the programme's own IP terms could not be read.

Vendor no Aave v3 source. Its BUSL-1.1 additional use grant forbids use that "directly or indirectly" facilitates migration of funds from the Aave ecosystem, Aave v3 is live on BSC, and a yield or health-factor comparison agent sits close to that clause. Read Aave through the deployed ABI, and build health factor on Venus (BSD-3-Clause, no use restriction, deeper on BSC).

Copy no code from pancakeswap/erc-8183-example (no licence anywhere, so no permission) and none from pancakeswap/pancakeswap-ai (MIT asserted twice, LICENSE file absent). Read both to learn the call sequences, then write against ERC-8183 and ERC-8004, which are CC0.

Do not put a compliance check behind a single free RPC. The Allnodes terms behind publicnode forbid "data mining, robots, scraping", cap liability at the amount paid, and reject JSON-RPC batching with HTTP 403, so configure a batch-capable fallback and refuse to quote when both endpoints are unreachable.

verified.claim: A marketplace that only lists and matches, with parties settling elsewhere, is not a money transmitter under FinCEN regulations

design_implications: Never take custody and never sit in the payment flow. The marketplace quotes, the buyer signs, the facilitator or an escrow whose keys we do not hold moves value, and the platform fee is a split inside that same settlement. This is the FIN-2019-G001 forum position, and running our own x402 facilitator that collects then remits crosses into the money-transmitter definition.

Screen on the quote path with four keyless calls and re-run at settlement: isSanctioned on 0x40C57923924B5c5c5455c48D93317139ADDaC8fb, membership of the locally ingested SDN EVM set with the chain tag ignored, frozen(payer) and frozen(payee), and paused() on the settlement token. Run all four on the buyer, the seller's payee and the agent's registered wallet, since setAgentWallet can change the payee independently.

One screening source is provably not enough. 20 of the 42 BSC-active SDN addresses are invisible to the oracle, and only one SDN address carries a BNB tag (and it is not even EVM-format), so ignore OFAC's chain tag entirely and screen the union of all 91 0x addresses plus the oracle.

Handle results asymmetrically. A direct-counterparty hit is a hard block, logged, with a reason shown. Graph proximity, an issuer freeze on an unrelated address, or a partial match is a review flag and never an automatic action, because inbound taint lets an attacker pick who gets frozen.

Refuse to quote when the escrow token is frozen or paused, before the user commits. Two extra eth_calls turn a mid-job failure into a clean pre-quote refusal, and they are the only visibility anyone has into the GENIUS Act freeze layer. Guard the calls, because BSC-USD implements neither.

Build every agent output as one of four shapes: measurement, comparison on published criteria, user-parameterised simulation, or mechanical execution of a user-set rule. That keeps the product outside the MiCA and MiFID II definition of advice by construction rather than by disclaimer. Show the downside beside the upside, and attach the block and source to every number.

Never claim independence. A marketplace takes a sell-side fee, which is a third-party benefit under MiCA Art 81(3)(b), so publish the fee and the ranking methodology and state that neither is advice, instead of asserting independence while taking a listing fee.

Present as a broker and behave like one: operator named on every listing and receipt, published ranking methodology, no outcome warranties, no first-party framing of third-party agents. DSA Art 6(3) removes the consumer-protection safe harbour exactly where a platform looks like the seller, and "official marketplace" framing plus heavy curation is that fact pattern.

Pin the keccak of the agent's reviewed metadata and card at review time and re-check on a schedule, treating drift as a new listing. setAgentURI, setMetadata and setAgentWallet are owner-callable at any time, so without this, "reviewed" has no referent.

Only count ERC-8004 feedback bound to a settled job with a distinct payer, show the settled-job count beside the score, label unbound feedback as unverified, and publish the rule. UCPD Annex I 23b and 23c make the alternative unfair in all circumstances, and this is simultaneously the honest answer to Data Quality on the rubric.

Collect nothing that creates the identification link. Wallet signature as the only account, no email, no IP joined to an address, no identity documents until an obligation attaches. The EDPB says an address becomes personal data when our own database can link it, and both DSA Art 10(2)(b) and 18 USC 2703(c)(2) only reach data already collected, so minimal collection is a compliance asset rather than a gap.

Keep nothing personal on-chain beyond what the transaction inherently carries: hashes and ids, never briefs or contents. EDPB Recommendation 11 says that if a technical deletion or anonymisation path does not exist then no personal data should go on the chain at all.

Emit a statement of reasons automatically from every enforcement action, with an onChainEffect field that reads "none", because the ERC-8004 registries are append-only and takedown means delisting from our index. The privacy notice and the takedown policy must say that in the same words.

Build both complaint systems, not one: DSA Art 20 for buyers (electronic, free, six-month window, reversal path) and P2B Art 11 for sellers, plus a public page rendering the four Art 11(4) statistics. TermiX, the incumbent in the sponsor track, publishes no terms at all, so clearing this bar is cheap and visible.

Split the licence by entry versus contribution: SAND-1.0 on the marketplace app and the ranking implementation (the judged, forkable surface), Apache-2.0 on the compliance layer and the four reference agents (the pieces meant to be adopted), CC0 on any published schema, and a separate ADOPTION.md rather than a pre-assignment, since the programme's own IP terms could not be read.

Vendor no Aave v3 source. Its BUSL-1.1 additional use grant forbids use that "directly or indirectly" facilitates migration of funds from the Aave ecosystem, Aave v3 is live on BSC, and a yield or health-factor comparison agent sits close to that clause. Read Aave through the deployed ABI, and build health factor on Venus (BSD-3-Clause, no use restriction, deeper on BSC).

Copy no code from pancakeswap/erc-8183-example (no licence anywhere, so no permission) and none from pancakeswap/pancakeswap-ai (MIT asserted twice, LICENSE file absent). Read both to learn the call sequences, then write against ERC-8183 and ERC-8004, which are CC0.

Do not put a compliance check behind a single free RPC. The Allnodes terms behind publicnode forbid "data mining, robots, scraping", cap liability at the amount paid, and reject JSON-RPC batching with HTTP 403, so configure a batch-capable fallback and refuse to quote when both endpoints are unreachable.

design_implications: 8004scan is an enrichment source, not the index of record. The chain it indexes worst is the chain we are judged on. A submission whose agent list is a live proxy to api.8004scan.io shows a judge an empty or erroring page if the 57% failure window recurs during judging. Own the index, borrow the enrichment.

Build the mirror from BSC RPC. Token ids are dense from 0 to 334,876, tokenURI plus ownerOf reaches every agent with no third-party dependency, and 51% of records carry their metadata in an on-chain data: URI needing no HTTP fetch at all. Tail with Registered logs in small block windows. That yields a fresher and more complete index than the official scanner, which is demonstrable on screen rather than merely asserted.

Never plan a full backfill through the API. 3,035 pages of 100 at offsets costing up to 29 seconds, with a 20% to 57% error rate and mandatory retries, is a multi-hour job that can fail at page 2,000. Use created_after with sort_order=asc for the incremental tail only, never for history.

There is no way to learn that an existing agent changed. No updated_after filter, no agent webhook, no stream, and updated_at moves for reasons unrelated to content. Change detection has to be ours: hash the tokenURI bytes per agent, watch URIUpdated and MetadataSet logs, re-fetch on a hash change. This is also what makes a 'live' claim defensible in a demo.

Classification into the four mandated categories has to be ours, and it is buildable. OASF covers 0.12% of BSC and contains nothing about rebalancing, grids, yield or health factors, while semantic search returns junk for all four prompts with inert tuning knobs. Full-text search finds the right agents in every one of the four, so seed the taxonomy from keyword recall over name, description and service metadata, then rank on our own evidence rather than total_score.

The scarce signal is a verified reachable endpoint and there are five on BSC, four of them one rival's build. Any marketplace whose ranking rewards a working endpoint will look nearly empty on 8004scan's data and will be right. Probe the A2A card and MCP manifest ourselves, timestamp it, and show the timestamp.

Use the unauthenticated verify trigger as a product feature. POST /agents/verify-endpoint/{chain}/{token} needs no key and is capped at once per hour per agent, so we can make the official scanner re-verify every agent we list, then cite its verdict on our profile page. Read the outcome from endpoint_verification_error and updated_at, never from endpoint_last_checked_at which the run does not touch.

Do not display 8004scan's freshness fields as freshness. health_score 100.0 on an agent with a broken certificate, endpoint_last_checked_at frozen at 2026-05-20 through a check that ran today, last_parsed_at on a mutable HTTPS URL. Show our own probe timestamp, and where we surface theirs, label it with their date.

Treat their score as a citation, not our ranking. The v5 weights are public (engagement 0.30, service 0.25, publisher 0.20, compliance 0.15, momentum 0.10, band 30 to 55), and engagement at 0.30 dominates on a chain where 27 addresses wrote every feedback. Publishing '8004scan score: 30.5 (their algorithm, their date)' beside our own evidence-based rank is both honest and a differentiator.

agent_wallet cannot be the payment destination. It defaults to the owner for every agent, so paying it pays the registrant. Get the payout target from an x402 challenge or explicit onboarding, and treat a non-null agent_wallet as zero evidence.

Reputation has to be earned inside our own product. 11,780 BSC feedbacks with zero today, score null in 99% of rows, no comments, 27 submitters, zero validations. The upside: appendResponse on the Reputation Registry is open to anyone, so our verdicts can be written back on chain, and /ipfs/fetch recovers the evidence behind a feedback_uri 8004scan never parsed.

Client engineering rules, each earned this pass: set a User-Agent (the default Python one gets a Cloudflare 403 even with a valid key), retry every 5xx with backoff (the same URL flaps 200/500/404), never trust a 404 as absence (cross-check ownerOf), handle both response envelopes, cap limit at 100, do not read rate-limit headers off a 500 (they are absent), use /api/v1/chains as the liveness probe and never /status/summary.

Mint the key headlessly in CI on the operator's identity wallet, not a throwaway, because the Pro grant form asks for the wallet tied to the account. File the form for the AltLayer track optics knowing it buys no throughput we do not already measure.

Keep what is genuinely good and costly to rebuild: cross_chain_links with verification_status, the field_sources provenance map, the parse_status issue codes (WA040 for mutable metadata, IA027/IA028 for non-standard OASF), publisher certification tiers, the public /ipfs/fetch gateway fan-out, chain_stats for cross-chain context, and the /status/* family which is the only honest freshness disclosure in the ecosystem. Cite them, cache them, never block a page render on them.

POST /agents/verify-endpoint/{chain}/{token} needs no key and is capped at once per hour per agent, so we can make the official scanner re-verify every agent we list, then cite its verdict on our profile page. Do not display 8004scan's freshness fields as freshness. health_score 100.0 on an agent with a broken certificate, endpoint_last_checked_at frozen at 2026-05-20 through a check that ran today, last_parsed_at on a mutable HTTPS URL. Show our own probe timestamp, and where we surface theirs, label it with their date.

Treat their score as a citation, not our ranking. The v5 weights are public (engagement 0.30, service 0.25, publisher 0.20, compliance 0.15, momentum 0.10, band 30 to 55), and engagement at 0.30 dominates on a chain where 27 addresses wrote every feedback. Publishing '8004scan score: 30.5 (their algorithm, their date)' beside our own evidence-based rank is both honest and a differentiator.

agent_wallet cannot be the payment destination. It defaults to the owner for every agent, so paying it pays the registrant. Get the payout target from an x402 challenge or explicit onboarding, and treat a non-null agent_wallet as zero evidence.

Reputation has to be earned inside our own product. 11,780 BSC feedbacks with zero today, score null in 99% of rows, no comments, 27 submitters, zero validations. The upside: appendResponse on the Reputation Registry is open to anyone, so our verdicts can be written back on chain, and /ipfs/fetch recovers the evidence behind a feedback_uri 8004scan never parsed.

Client engineering rules, each earned this pass: set a User-Agent (the default Python one gets a Cloudflare 403 even with a valid key), retry every 5xx with backoff (the same URL flaps 200/500/404), never trust a 404 as absence (cross-check ownerOf), handle both response envelopes, cap limit at 100, do not read rate-limit headers off a 500 (they are absent), use /api/v1/chains as the liveness probe and never /status/summary.

Mint the key headlessly in CI on the operator's identity wallet, not a throwaway, because the Pro grant form asks for the wallet tied to the account. File the form for the AltLayer track optics knowing it buys no throughput we do not already measure.

Keep what is genuinely good and costly to rebuild: cross_chain_links with verification_status, the field_sources provenance map, the parse_status issue codes (WA040 for mutable metadata, IA027/IA028 for non-standard OASF), publisher certification tiers, the public /ipfs/fetch gateway fan-out, chain_stats for cross-chain context, and the /status/* family which is the only honest freshness disclosure in the ecosystem. Cite them, cache them, never block a page render on them.

design_implications: Verdict: ERC-8183 is a BONUS for the main track, worth taking, not a requirement and not a distraction. Nothing in Functionality, Data Quality or Agent Diversity requires it, but it is the only mechanism that turns "hire this agent" into a verifiable state change a judge can check with one getJob call. Budget it as a thin layer over a marketplace that is already complete without it, because the four mandated categories are the stated bar and category depth wins any time conflict.

The smallest honest Altana-bonus version is two jobs. One mainnet job funded from an Altana wallet against a real Agent Studio seller address (evaluator = router, hook = router, registerJob the whitelisted policy, setBudget, approve the KERNEL, fund) and one testnet job driven all the way to COMPLETED, where the 900-second window closes the loop inside a single sitting. Together the claim is: the hire is real on mainnet, the settlement path is proven end to end. Neither rival's mainnet jobs in my sample had settled.

Timing: build closes 2026-09-09 and judging runs to 2026-09-23, so a mainnet job submitted on 2026-09-08 becomes settleable around 2026-09-15, mid-judging. Show it as in-flight with the auto-approval date on the page, cite the job id, then run settle on the 15th. Never label it COMPLETED before it is.

A zero-cost mainnet hire is possible and honest: ZeroBudget() guards jobHasBudget rather than the amount, so an explicit setBudget(jobId, 0) then fund(jobId, 0) produces a real escrow of zero that settles. 10 of 62 completed jobs in my sample did this. Use it where the deliverable is a read-only report, use a real budget where the point is that money moved, and never describe a zero-budget job as a paid hire.

Do not display jobCounter as marketplace volume. 285 of 288 jobs in a whole-range sample were one bulk campaign against 4 providers, and the counter did not move at all across 1714 seconds. Show per-provider and per-category counts over a named window instead.

Index by provider address then join to ERC-8004 via registry.ownerOf(agentId) == job.provider. That held for both rivals and it is what produces the per-agent employment history the TermiX rubric calls track record. Brain on BNB already advertises this, so it will be compared.

Parse all three deliverable conventions or two thirds of live sellers render blank: {"deliverable_url": ...} hashed keccak256(canonicalJson(manifest)), an inline JSON document hashed sha256(raw bytes), and empty optParams which is simply not retrievable. Label which rule matched rather than showing an unqualified "verified".

Verify the negotiation quote and show the result. 170 of 314 recent jobs carry one, the recipe reproduces exactly, and it separates "the seller agreed this price" from "the buyer typed a number". Show the recovered signer, whether it equals the provider, and whether the quote had expired at the funding block.

The 7-day mainnet window shapes the UI: FUNDED and SUBMITTED must be first-class states with a countdown to auto-approval, a dispute button while the window is open and a claim-refund button after expiredAt. Treating COMPLETED as the only success state makes the product look broken on its own happy path.

Run a settler. settle is permissionless, nobody is obliged to call it, and 28,326 jobs sit in flight on the router right now. Settling our own jobs the moment the window elapses is a real service that is cheap to run and easy to demonstrate.

Read the testnet policy address from the current SDK at build time and assert router.policyWhitelist(policy) is true before the first hire. The address already changed once between our 2026-08-27 capture and today, and anything pinned to 0x4F4678D4439feC812Ac7674Bb3Efb4C8f5Fb78A6 dies at registerJob with PolicyNotWhitelisted().

canonicalJson is load-bearing and is not JSON.stringify: keys sorted at every depth, compact separators, every non-ASCII code unit escaped as \uXXXX so it matches Python json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":")). Both SDKs warn that plain stringify breaks cross-SDK verification for any accent, CJK or emoji.

Custom policy on mainnet is off the table (owner-only whitelist, exactly one policy). The available lever is a custom IACPHook plus our own evaluator, since the kernel enforces only ERC-165 on the hook and nothing on the evaluator, but that means leaving the optimistic settlement and the 3-of-5 dispute panel behind and issuing our own attestations. Knowing it exists matters more than using it.

Read platformFeeBP rather than hardcoding zero. It is 0 today with MAX_PLATFORM_FEE_BP 1000 and setPlatformFee is owner-only on an upgradeable proxy, so any net-to-seller figure computed from a constant will silently go wrong.

From a session key the five-call batch becomes four calls plus a pre-provisioned allowance: Altana deliberately grants sessions no ERC-20 approve permission, so the admin must call setErc8183Allowance(paymentToken, commerce, cap) beforehand and quote signing needs approveQuoteSignatureChecker(session, commerce) first.

design_implications: Verdict: ERC-8183 is a BONUS for the main track, worth taking, not a requirement and not a distraction. Nothing in Functionality, Data Quality or Agent Diversity requires it, but it is the only mechanism that turns "hire this agent" into a verifiable state change a judge can check with one getJob call. Budget it as a thin layer over a marketplace that is already complete without it, because the four mandated categories are the stated bar and category depth wins any time conflict.

The smallest honest Altana-bonus version is two jobs. One mainnet job funded from an Altana wallet against a real Agent Studio seller address (evaluator = router, hook = router, registerJob the whitelisted policy, setBudget, approve the KERNEL, fund) and one testnet job driven all the way to COMPLETED, where the 900-second window closes the loop inside a single sitting. Together the claim is: the hire is real on mainnet, the settlement path is proven end to end. Neither rival's mainnet jobs in my sample had settled.

Timing: build closes 2026-09-09 and judging runs to 2026-09-23, so a mainnet job submitted on 2026-09-08 becomes settleable around 2026-09-15, mid-judging. Show it as in-flight with the auto-approval date on the page, cite the job id, then run settle on the 15th. Never label it COMPLETED before it is.

A zero-cost mainnet hire is possible and honest: ZeroBudget() guards jobHasBudget rather than the amount, so an explicit setBudget(jobId, 0) then fund(jobId, 0) produces a real escrow of zero that settles. 10 of 62 completed jobs in my sample did this. Use it where the deliverable is a read-only report, use a real budget where the point is that money moved, and never describe a zero-budget job as a paid hire.

Do not display jobCounter as marketplace volume. 285 of 288 jobs in a whole-range sample were one bulk campaign against 4 providers, and the counter did not move at all across 1714 seconds. Show per-provider and per-category counts over a named window instead.

Index by provider address then join to ERC-8004 via registry.ownerOf(agentId) == job.provider. That held for both rivals and it is what produces the per-agent employment history the TermiX rubric calls track record. Brain on BNB already advertises this, so it will be compared.

Parse all three deliverable conventions or two thirds of live sellers render blank: {"deliverable_url": ...} hashed keccak256(canonicalJson(manifest)), an inline JSON document hashed sha256(raw bytes), and empty optParams which is simply not retrievable. Label which rule matched rather than showing an unqualified "verified".

Verify the negotiation quote and show the result. 170 of 314 recent jobs carry one, the recipe reproduces exactly, and it separates "the seller agreed this price" from "the buyer typed a number". Show the recovered signer, whether it equals the provider, and whether the quote had expired at the funding block.

The 7-day mainnet window shapes the UI: FUNDED and SUBMITTED must be first-class states with a countdown to auto-approval, a dispute button while the window is open and a claim-refund button after expiredAt. Treating COMPLETED as the only success state makes the product look broken on its own happy path.

Run a settler. settle is permissionless, nobody is obliged to call it, and 28,326 jobs sit in flight on the router right now. Settling our own jobs the moment the window elapses is a real service that is cheap to run and easy to demonstrate.

Read the testnet policy address from the current SDK at build time and assert router.policyWhitelist(policy) is true before the first hire. The address already changed once between our 2026-08-27 capture and today, and anything pinned to 0x4F4678D4439feC812Ac7674Bb3Efb4C8f5Fb78A6 dies at registerJob with PolicyNotWhitelisted().

canonicalJson is load-bearing and is not JSON.stringify: keys sorted at every depth, compact separators, every non-ASCII code unit escaped as \uXXXX so it matches Python json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":")). Both SDKs warn that plain stringify breaks cross-SDK verification for any accent, CJK or emoji.

Custom policy on mainnet is off the table (owner-only whitelist, exactly one policy). The available lever is a custom IACPHook plus our own evaluator, since the kernel enforces only ERC-165 on the hook and nothing on the evaluator, but that means leaving the optimistic settlement and the 3-of-5 dispute panel behind and issuing our own attestations. Knowing it exists matters more than using it.

Read platformFeeBP rather than hardcoding zero. It is 0 today with MAX_PLATFORM_FEE_BP 1000 and setPlatformFee is owner-only on an upgradeable proxy, so any net-to-seller figure computed from a constant will silently go wrong.

From a session key the five-call batch becomes four calls plus a pre-provisioned allowance: Altana deliberately grants sessions no ERC-20 approve permission, so the admin must call setErc8183Allowance(paymentToken, commerce, cap) beforehand and quote signing needs approveQuoteSignatureChecker(session, commerce) first.

journal_result.headline: Steam counts a review toward a product's score only if the account bought the product on Steam while letting anyone who launched it still write one, and that verified-transaction-only split plus a Bayesian shrink toward a per-category prior is the cheapest defence against a catalogue of 287,029 registered agents where almost none transact.

design_implications: The listing gate is a live call, not a review queue. GitHub Marketplace proves a mechanical gate scales, and npm gives the standard to apply to a catalogue of shells: a listing is squatted if it "has no genuine function". One successful round trip against the declared capability is the only gate that changes the 287,029 number.

Make each of the four mandated categories a document, not a string: definition, required input and output contract, the metric it is scored on, plus three to five hand-picked exemplars. Copy the Hugging Face task-object shape and Apple's category prose together. This makes miscategorisation reviewable and makes "equally deep in all four" checkable.

Score with a Bayesian shrink toward a per-category prior (measured: 0.8095 for one perfect job, 0.9000 for twenty, against an 0.80 prior). Reserve the Wilson lower bound for the risk gate. This defeats the single-fake-review attack with arithmetic, with no fraud detection needed.
Count only paid, settled jobs toward the score while letting anyone comment. That is Steam's exact split, and on BSC the settled payment is already the primitive, so it costs one join.

Weight by transaction size, decay with a published half life, and converge back to the prior on inactivity rather than to zero. Upwork weights by earnings, Fiverr by order value and recency, and neither punishes inactivity.

Zero-weight feedback from inside the payer's own funding cluster, using the published one-hop provenance heuristic plus the 25-event habitual threshold as a flag. Record it anyway: deleting it looks like suppression under 16 CFR 465.7(b), and zero weight keeps it out of the score.

Build assignment as OpenRouter's policy with success rate substituted for price: 30-second outage memory, randomised weighted pick among the qualified, demote on failure rather than exclude, rolling percentile window for performance facets, hard constraints for spend caps and soft preferences for latency. It is the only mechanism here that is production-proven, published in full, and buildable in an afternoon.

Add Thompson sampling on top only if time allows. Ten lines with Beta counters per agent per category, best-in-class on real ad data, and specifically robust to the delayed rewards an agent job produces. Fall back to epsilon-greedy with a published exploration percentage.

Reserve the Dutch auction for price discovery, not supplier selection. UniswapX's linear decay plus the exclusivity override fits a buyer stating a budget range. Filter on eligibility first, or the fastest responder wins every job regardless of quality.

Escrow must auto-release on silence: fund first, submit through the platform, short review window, auto-release on expiry, one restart per change request, then dispute. Without auto-release, escrow is a hostage mechanism.

Adopt Stripe's dispute evidence schema renamed for agent work, grouped as delivered, used, promised, ruled, said, rebutted, plus due_by, submission_count, past_due and a prevented state for auto-refunds that never become disputes. On-chain this schema is unusually strong because delivery and payment evidence are both hashes.

Emit a statement of reasons on every adverse action including demotions and payment suspensions, using the DSA Article 17(3) elements. A machine-readable reasons log is a differentiator here, not a compliance chore, and it is what makes a ranking claim auditable.
Give appeals a published window and a different decider, with new evidence only as the standard. Six months is the DSA floor, 30 days is eBay's practice.

Suspend abusive reporters on the same terms as abusive listers, using DSA Article 23's symmetry and its four weighing factors. A takedown button with no misuse rule will be used as a weapon against rival agents.

Label operator-built agents, rank them under the identical formula with no bonus term, and report first-party and third-party counts separately so "four categories deeply covered" never quietly means "four categories we built". P2B Article 7 supplies the disclosure wording, DMA Article 6(5) the no-favouritism wording, and the closest comparable marketplace does not do it.

Publish the ranking parameters and the thresholds, withhold the coefficients. P2B Article 5(1) plus the 5(6) carve-out is the explicit licence for this, and it is exactly what Fiverr, Steam and IMDb all do.

Instrument the ranking with a randomised holdout from day one. Upwork's placebo auction is the only design found that produces a causal number about whether the matching helps. Even a 2% holdout yields an honest claim instead of a screenshot.

Cap what an unproven supplier may list rather than refusing to list it (Fiverr allows 4 Gigs to a New freelancer, and gates Level 1 at 5 orders, 3 unique clients, $400 earned plus a 4.4 rating), and normalise scores within a price or category peer group so four mandated categories become four leaderboards rather than one.

Attach a per-listing machine-readable safety verdict with three levels, and warn rather than delete on a hit. Hugging Face's securityRepoStatus.filesWithIssues[].level is the shape, and it is far more useful to a browsing buyer than a listing that silently vanished.

Skip the mechanisms that do not fit a four-day build and publish the policy instead: human editorial curation (replace with per-category exemplars), a trusted-flagger program, a reviewer trust graph (replace with a counterparty discount list), on-chain Dutch auctions, contextual bandits with feature engineering, and real-time batched matching that a light load will never justify.

design_implications: The listing gate is a live call, not a review queue. GitHub Marketplace proves a mechanical gate scales, and npm gives the standard to apply to a catalogue of shells: a listing is squatted if it "has no genuine function". One successful round trip against the declared capability is the only gate that changes the 287,029 number.

Make each of the four mandated categories a document, not a string: definition, required input and output contract, the metric it is scored on, plus three to five hand-picked exemplars. Copy the Hugging Face task-object shape and Apple's category prose together. This makes miscategorisation reviewable and makes "equally deep in all four" checkable.

Score with a Bayesian shrink toward a per-category prior (measured: 0.8095 for one perfect job, 0.9000 for twenty, against an 0.80 prior). Reserve the Wilson lower bound for the risk gate. This defeats the single-fake-review attack with arithmetic, with no fraud detection needed.
Count only paid, settled jobs toward the score while letting anyone comment. That is Steam's exact split, and on BSC the settled payment is already the primitive, so it costs one join.

Weight by transaction size, decay with a published half life, and converge back to the prior on inactivity rather than to zero. Upwork weights by earnings, Fiverr by order value and recency, and neither punishes inactivity.

Zero-weight feedback from inside the payer's own funding cluster, using the published one-hop provenance heuristic plus the 25-event habitual threshold as a flag. Record it anyway: deleting it looks like suppression under 16 CFR 465.7(b), and zero weight keeps it out of the score.

Build assignment as OpenRouter's policy with success rate substituted for price: 30-second outage memory, randomised weighted pick among the qualified, demote on failure rather than exclude, rolling percentile window for performance facets, hard constraints for spend caps and soft preferences for latency. It is the only mechanism here that is production-proven, published in full, and buildable in an afternoon.

Add Thompson sampling on top only if time allows. Ten lines with Beta counters per agent per category, best-in-class on real ad data, and specifically robust to the delayed rewards an agent job produces. Fall back to epsilon-greedy with a published exploration percentage.

Reserve the Dutch auction for price discovery, not supplier selection. UniswapX's linear decay plus the exclusivity override fits a buyer stating a budget range. Filter on eligibility first, or the fastest responder wins every job regardless of quality.

Escrow must auto-release on silence: fund first, submit through the platform, short review window, auto-release on expiry, one restart per change request, then dispute. Without auto-release, escrow is a hostage mechanism.

Adopt Stripe's dispute evidence schema renamed for agent work, grouped as delivered, used, promised, ruled, said, rebutted, plus due_by, submission_count, past_due and a prevented state for auto-refunds that never become disputes. On-chain this schema is unusually strong because delivery and payment evidence are both hashes.

Emit a statement of reasons on every adverse action including demotions and payment suspensions, using the DSA Article 17(3) elements. A machine-readable reasons log is a differentiator here, not a compliance chore, and it is what makes a ranking claim auditable.
Give appeals a published window and a different decider, with new evidence only as the standard. Six months is the DSA floor, 30 days is eBay's practice.

Suspend abusive reporters on the same terms as abusive listers, using DSA Article 23's symmetry and its four weighing factors. A takedown button with no misuse rule will be used as a weapon against rival agents.

Label operator-built agents, rank them under the identical formula with no bonus term, and report first-party and third-party counts separately so "four categories deeply covered" never quietly means "four categories we built". P2B Article 7 supplies the disclosure wording, DMA Article 6(5) the no-favouritism wording, and the closest comparable marketplace does not do it.

Publish the ranking parameters and the thresholds, withhold the coefficients. P2B Article 5(1) plus the 5(6) carve-out is the explicit licence for this, and it is exactly what Fiverr, Steam and IMDb all do.

Instrument the ranking with a randomised holdout from day one. Upwork's placebo auction is the only design found that produces a causal number about whether the matching helps. Even a 2% holdout yields an honest claim instead of a screenshot.

Cap what an unproven supplier may list rather than refusing to list it (Fiverr allows 4 Gigs to a New freelancer, and gates Level 1 at 5 orders, 3 unique clients, $400 earned plus a 4.4 rating), and normalise scores within a price or category peer group so four mandated categories become four leaderboards rather than one.

Attach a per-listing machine-readable safety verdict with three levels, and warn rather than delete on a hit. Hugging Face's securityRepoStatus.filesWithIssues[].level is the shape, and it is far more useful to a browsing buyer than a listing that silently vanished.

Skip the mechanisms that do not fit a four-day build and publish the policy instead: human editorial curation (replace with per-category exemplars), a trusted-flagger program, a reviewer trust graph (replace with a counterparty discount list), on-chain Dutch auctions, contextual bandits with feature engineering, and real-time batched matching that a light load will never justify.
